421	// wrapLines soft-wraps content so no line exceeds width runes.
422	func wrapLines(content string, width int) string {
423		if width <= 0 {
424			return content
425		}
426		lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
427		out := make([]string, 0, len(lines))
428		for _, line := range lines {
429			runes := []rune(line)
430			if len(runes) <= width {
431				out = append(out, line)
432				continue
433			}
434			for len(runes) > width {
435				out = append(out, string(runes[:width]))
436				runes = runes[width:]
437			}
438			if len(runes) > 0 {
439				out = append(out, string(runes))
440			}
441		}
442		return strings.Join(out, "\n")
443	}

611	// cycleSort cycles through sort options: each column asc then desc, then next column
612	func (m Model) cycleSort() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
613		if m.sortAsc {
614			m.sortAsc = false
615		} else {
616			m.sortAsc = true
617			nextIdx := 0
618			for i, col := range sortableColumns {
619				if col == m.sortColumn {
620					nextIdx = (i + 1) % len(sortableColumns)
621					break
622				}
623			}
624			m.sortColumn = sortableColumns[nextIdx]
625		}
626		m.updateTable()
627		return m, nil
628	}

630	// sortedContainers returns containers sorted by the current sort column
631	func (m *Model) sortedContainers(containers []docker.Container) []docker.Container {
632		sorted := make([]docker.Container, len(containers))
633		copy(sorted, containers)
634	
635		sort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {
636			a, b := sorted[i], sorted[j]
637	
638			var less bool
639			switch m.sortColumn {
640			case sortByImage:
641				less = strings.ToLower(a.Image) < strings.ToLower(b.Image)
642			case sortByCPU:
643				less = a.CPUPercent < b.CPUPercent
644			case sortByMem:
645				less = a.MemPercent < b.MemPercent
646			case sortByNetRX:
647				less = a.NetRX < b.NetRX
648			case sortByNetTX:
649				less = a.NetTX < b.NetTX
650			case sortByBlockRX:
651				less = a.BlockRX < b.BlockRX
652			case sortByBlockTX:
653				less = a.BlockTX < b.BlockTX
654			case sortByCreated:
655				less = a.CreatedAt < b.CreatedAt
656			default: // sortByName
657				less = strings.ToLower(a.Name) < strings.ToLower(b.Name)
658			}
659	
660			if m.sortAsc {
661				return less
662			}
663			return !less
664		})
665	
666		return sorted
667	}

669	// formatNetBytes formats bytes into a compact human-readable string (e.g. "1.2kB", "3.4MB")
670	func formatNetBytes(b int64) string {
671		switch {
672		case b >= 1e9:
673			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fGB", float64(b)/1e9)
674		case b >= 1e6:
675			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fMB", float64(b)/1e6)
676		case b >= 1e3:
677			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fkB", float64(b)/1e3)
678		default:
679			return fmt.Sprintf("%dB", b)
680		}
681	}

701	// formatMemUsage parses docker MemUsage "150MiB / 7.776GiB" into compact "150M/8G"
702	func formatMemUsage(memUsage string) string {
703		parts := strings.SplitN(memUsage, "/", 2)
704		if len(parts) != 2 {
705			return memUsage
706		}
707		used := formatMemValue(strings.TrimSpace(parts[0]))
708		total := formatMemValue(strings.TrimSpace(parts[1]))
709		return used + "/" + total
710	}
711	
712	// formatMemValue converts "150MiB" -> "150M", "7.776GiB" -> "8G", "512KiB" -> "512K"
713	func formatMemValue(val string) string {
714		val = strings.TrimSpace(val)
715	
716		// Try each unit suffix
717		for _, suffix := range []struct {
718			docker string
719			short  string
720			isGig  bool
721		}{
722			{"GiB", "G", true},
723			{"MiB", "M", false},
724			{"KiB", "K", false},
725			{"B", "B", false},
726		} {
727			if strings.HasSuffix(val, suffix.docker) {
728				numStr := strings.TrimSuffix(val, suffix.docker)
729				num, err := strconv.ParseFloat(numStr, 64)
730				if err != nil {
731					return val
732				}
733				if suffix.isGig {
734					// Round GiB to nearest integer
735					return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f%s", num, suffix.short)
736				}
737				// For MiB/KiB, show integer
738				return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f%s", num, suffix.short)
739			}
740		}
741		return val
742	}

744	// relativeTime converts a docker CreatedAt timestamp to a human-readable relative time
745	func relativeTime(createdAt string) string {
746		// Docker format: "2026-02-07 12:14:13 +0100 CET"
747		// Try parsing with timezone name suffix
748		t, err := time.Parse("2006-01-02 15:04:05 -0700 MST", createdAt)
749		if err != nil {
750			// Try without timezone name
751			t, err = time.Parse("2006-01-02 15:04:05 -0700", createdAt)
752			if err != nil {
753				return createdAt
754			}
755		}
756	
757		return theme.TimeAgo(t) // Rule 127
758	}

760	// updateTable rebuilds the table rows from the current container list
761	func (m *Model) updateTable() {
762		sorted := m.sortedContainers(m.filteredContainers())
763		rows := make([]table.Row, 0, len(sorted))
764	
765		for _, c := range sorted {
766			cpuStr := "-"
767			memStr := "-"
768			rxStr := "-"
769			txStr := "-"
770			blkRXStr := "-"
771			blkTXStr := "-"
772	
773			if c.State == "running" {
774				cpuStr = fmt.Sprintf("%.1f%%", c.CPUPercent)
775				memStr = formatMemUsage(c.MemUsage)
776	
777				if c.NetIO != "" {
778					rxStr = formatNetBytes(c.NetRX)
779					txStr = formatNetBytes(c.NetTX)
780				}
781				if c.BlockIO != "" {
782					blkRXStr = formatNetBytes(c.BlockRX)
783					blkTXStr = formatNetBytes(c.BlockTX)
784				}
785			}
786	
787			imageWithState := stateIcon(c.State) + " " + c.Image
788	
789			rows = append(rows, table.Row{
790				c.Name,
791				imageWithState,
792				cpuStr,
793				memStr,
794				rxStr,
795				txStr,
796				blkRXStr,
797				blkTXStr,
798				relativeTime(c.CreatedAt),
799				c.Ports,
800			})
801		}
802	
803		// Update column headers with sort indicators
804		cols := m.containerTable.Columns()
805		if len(cols) >= 10 {
806			sortColIndex := map[sortField]int{
807				sortByName:    0,
808				sortByImage:   1,
809				sortByCPU:     2,
810				sortByMem:     3,
811				sortByNetRX:   4,
812				sortByNetTX:   5,
813				sortByBlockRX: 6,
814				sortByBlockTX: 7,
815				sortByCreated: 8,
816			}
817			baseTitles := map[int]string{
818				0: "Name", 1: "Image", 2: "CPU", 3: "Mem",
819				4: "Net RX", 5: "Net TX", 6: "Block RX", 7: "Block TX", 8: "Created",
820			}
821			for idx, title := range baseTitles {
822				cols[idx].Title = title
823			}
824			if idx, ok := sortColIndex[m.sortColumn]; ok {
825				arrow := " ▲"
826				if !m.sortAsc {
827					arrow = " ▼"
828				}
829				cols[idx].Title = baseTitles[idx] + arrow
830			}
831			m.containerTable.SetColumns(cols)
832		}
833	
834		m.containerTable.SetRows(rows)
835		m.refreshSelectionStyle()
836	}

838	// refreshSelectionStyle updates the table selection color to match the currently selected container's state
839	func (m *Model) refreshSelectionStyle() {
840		sorted := m.sortedContainers(m.filteredContainers())
841		cursor := m.containerTable.Cursor()
842		if cursor < 0 || cursor >= len(sorted) {
843			m.containerTable.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("normal"))
844			return
845		}
846		state := "normal"
847		if s := sorted[cursor].State; s == "exited" || s == "dead" {
848			state = "error"
849		}
850		m.containerTable.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState(state))
851	}

1	// Package datatable is the shared mechanism behind the application's tables.
2	//
3	// What was shared before was only the *look* — theme.DefaultTableStyles,
4	// TableStylesForState/ForSeverity, components.FilterBar, theme.TimeAgo. Column
5	// widths, sorting, sort arrows, filter matching, cursor clamping and
6	// cursor-to-object resolution were written out again in each of the fifteen
7	// tables, and drifted:
8	//
9	//   - Rule 116's width invariant is broken by five of the twelve copies, which
10	//     clamp per column after the remainder has been computed (see widths.go).
11	//   - Two of eight clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks; the rest leave
12	//     it dangling, and oci_resources compensates by jumping to the top on every
13	//     filter toggle, throwing away the scroll position.
14	//   - Nine getSelectedX() replay filter-then-sort by hand to map a cursor back
15	//     to an object, with nothing tying that ordering to the one the rows were
16	//     built from. If they drift, the action lands on the wrong object and says
17	//     nothing. That is the duplication worth removing on correctness grounds.
18	//
19	// Here the filtered, sorted slice is built once and kept, so Selected() cannot
20	// disagree with what is on screen, and Cell func(T) string gives styled text
21	// nowhere to go — Rule 122 by construction rather than by review.
22	package datatable
23	
24	import (
25		"slices"
26		"sort"
27		"strings"
28	
29		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/table"
30		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
31	
32		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
33		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
34	)
35	
36	// Column describes one column and how to get its value out of an item.
37	type Column[T any] struct {
38		Title string
39		// MinWidth is what the column asks for. It is a request, not a guarantee:
40		// when the terminal is too narrow for every request, the shortfall is
41		// shared out rather than each column defending its own floor.
42		MinWidth int
43		// Flex is the column's share of the space left over. 0 keeps it at
44		// MinWidth; the leftover is split between the flexible ones by weight.
45		Flex int
46		// Cell returns the text for this column. Plain text only: bubbles/table
47		// truncates with runewidth, which does not understand ANSI, so a styled
48		// string is cut mid-escape and bleeds over every row below it (Rule 122).
49		// Taking a string rather than a styled value is what makes that
50		// unexpressible here.
51		Cell func(T) string
52		// Less sorts by this column. Nil means the column cannot be sorted by, and
53		// `.` skips it.
54		Less func(a, b T) bool
55		// Search is what the text filter matches against. Nil means the column does
56		// not participate.
57		Search func(T) string
58	}
59	
60	// Config is everything a view has to say about its table.
61	type Config[T any] struct {
62		Columns []Column[T]
63		// Tokens are the toggle filters shown in the bar (Rule 136).
64		Tokens []components.FilterToken
65		// TokenMatch decides whether an item passes the active toggles. Nil means
66		// the toggles are ignored, which is only sensible with no Tokens.
67		TokenMatch func(item T, active map[string]bool) bool
68		// SortColumn is the column sorted by on open; -1 for no initial sort.
69		SortColumn int
70		// SelectedStyles returns the table styles to use while the given item is
71		// under the cursor — that is the only thing bubbles/table can vary per
72		// selection, and it is what containers and security each re-derived by
73		// hand. Returning a style rather than a state keyword is what keeps this
74		// package from having to know what a severity is. Nil means the default.
75		SelectedStyles func(T) table.Styles
76	}
77	
78	// Model is a table over a slice of T.
79	type Model[T any] struct {
80		cfg   Config[T]
81		table table.Model
82		bar   components.FilterBar
83	
84		items []T
85		// visible is the filtered, sorted slice the rows were built from. Selected()
86		// reads it rather than recomputing, so the cursor cannot point at one
87		// ordering while the screen shows another.
88		visible []T
89	
90		sortColumn int
91		sortDesc   bool
92		width      int
93	}
94	
95	// New builds a table from its configuration.
96	func New[T any](cfg Config[T]) Model[T] {
97		cols := make([]table.Column, len(cfg.Columns))
98		for i, c := range cfg.Columns {
99			cols[i] = table.Column{Title: c.Title, Width: c.MinWidth}
100		}
101		t := table.New(table.WithColumns(cols), table.WithFocused(true), table.WithHeight(10))
102		t.SetStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
103	
104		bar := components.NewFilterBar()
105		if len(cfg.Tokens) > 0 {
106			bar = components.NewFilterBarWithTokens(cfg.Tokens)
107		}
108	
109		m := Model[T]{cfg: cfg, table: t, bar: bar, sortColumn: cfg.SortColumn}
110		// The invariant the rest of the file rests on: sortColumn is either -1 or a
111		// column that can actually be sorted by. Settling it once here is what lets
112		// CycleSort and sorted() stop re-checking — and what stops `.` getting stuck
113		// flipping the direction of a column with no comparator.
114		if m.sortColumn >= len(cfg.Columns) || (m.sortColumn >= 0 && cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].Less == nil) {
115			m.sortColumn = -1
116		}
117		return m
118	}
119	
120	// SetItems replaces the contents. Filtering, sorting, row building and the
121	// cursor clamp all happen here and only here, which is what stops a cursor from
122	// being left pointing past the end — bubbles/table's SetRows does not clamp, and
123	// the stale cursor is invisible until the user presses a key.
124	func (m *Model[T]) SetItems(items []T) {
125		m.items = items
126		m.rebuild()
127	}
128	
129	// Items returns everything held, filtered or not.
130	func (m *Model[T]) Items() []T { return m.items }
131	
132	// Visible returns what is on screen, in the order it is on screen.
133	func (m *Model[T]) Visible() []T { return m.visible }
134	
135	// Selected returns the item under the cursor. The bool is false when there is
136	// nothing to select, which is the only case a caller has to handle.
137	func (m *Model[T]) Selected() (T, bool) {
138		cursor := m.table.Cursor()
139		if cursor < 0 || cursor >= len(m.visible) {
140			var zero T
141			return zero, false
142		}
143		return m.visible[cursor], true
144	}
145	
146	// Cursor returns the selected row index.
147	func (m *Model[T]) Cursor() int { return m.table.Cursor() }
148	
149	// GotoTop moves the cursor to the first row. Views that want the cursor reset
150	// on a change of scope — security resets it when the tab changes — call this
151	// explicitly, because SetItems deliberately does not.
152	func (m *Model[T]) GotoTop() { m.table.GotoTop() }
153	
154	// FilterBar exposes the bar for RenderFooter and GetFooterHeight (Rule 136).
155	func (m *Model[T]) FilterBar() *components.FilterBar { return &m.bar }
156	
157	// InEditMode reports whether the search field has the keyboard.
158	func (m *Model[T]) InEditMode() bool { return m.bar.InEditMode() }
159	
160	// Searchable reports whether anything can be filtered: a searchable column or a
161	// toggle token. Views use it to decide whether to advertise `/` (Rule 130).
162	func (m *Model[T]) Searchable() bool {
163		if len(m.cfg.Tokens) > 0 {
164			return true
165		}
166		for _, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
167			if c.Search != nil {
168				return true
169			}
170		}
171		return false
172	}
173	
174	// Table exposes the underlying table for rendering.
175	func (m *Model[T]) Table() *table.Model { return &m.table }
176	
177	// View renders the table.
178	func (m *Model[T]) View() string { return m.table.View() }
179	
180	// SetHeight sets the number of rows shown.
181	func (m *Model[T]) SetHeight(h int) { m.table.SetHeight(max(h, 1)) }
182	
183	// Focus and Blur move the keyboard between two tables sharing a viewport, which
184	// is what the status view does with its monitors and its certificates.
185	func (m *Model[T]) Focus() {
186		m.table.Focus()
187		m.applyStyles()
188	}
189	
190	func (m *Model[T]) Blur() {
191		m.table.Blur()
192		m.table.SetStyles(theme.BlurredTableStyles())
193	}
194	
195	// Resize recomputes the column widths for a viewport of this width (Rule 116).
196	// The width passed is the full viewport width, borders included; the borders and
197	// the per-cell padding are subtracted here so no caller has to remember to.
198	func (m *Model[T]) Resize(width, height int) {
199		m.width = width
200		widths := solveWidths(m.cfg.Columns, availableFor(width, len(m.cfg.Columns)))
201	
202		cols := m.table.Columns()
203		for i := range cols {
204			cols[i].Width = widths[i]
205			cols[i].Title = m.titleFor(i)
206		}
207		m.table.SetColumns(cols)
208		m.bar.Resize(width)
209		if height > 0 {
210			m.SetHeight(height)
211		}
212	}
213	
214	// titleFor returns a column's header, with a sort arrow on the active one.
215	func (m *Model[T]) titleFor(i int) string {
216		if i != m.sortColumn {
217			return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title
218		}
219		if m.sortDesc {
220			return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title + " ▼"
221		}
222		return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title + " ▲"
223	}
224	
225	// CycleSort advances the sort: ascending, descending, then on to the next
226	// sortable column (Rule 111's `.`). Returns to no sort after the last one when
227	// the table opened unsorted, so the original order stays reachable.
228	func (m *Model[T]) CycleSort() {
229		sortable := m.sortableColumns()
230		if len(sortable) == 0 {
231			return
232		}
233		switch {
234		case m.sortColumn < 0:
235			m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc = sortable[0], false
236		case !m.sortDesc:
237			m.sortDesc = true
238		default:
239			m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc = m.nextSortable(sortable), false
240		}
241		m.rebuild()
242		m.Resize(m.width, 0) // the arrow moved
243	}
244	
245	// nextSortable returns the column after the current one, wrapping to the first —
246	// or to -1 when the table opened unsorted, so "no sort" is a stop on the cycle.
247	//
248	// slices.Index rather than a loop with a trailing fallback: the current column
249	// is always in sortable (New guarantees it), and a fallback that cannot run is
250	// a branch nothing can ever check.
251	func (m *Model[T]) nextSortable(sortable []int) int {
252		if at := slices.Index(sortable, m.sortColumn); at+1 < len(sortable) {
253			return sortable[at+1]
254		}
255		if m.cfg.SortColumn < 0 {
256			return -1
257		}
258		return sortable[0]
259	}
260	
261	func (m *Model[T]) sortableColumns() []int {
262		var out []int
263		for i, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
264			if c.Less != nil {
265				out = append(out, i)
266			}
267		}
268		return out
269	}
270	
271	// SortState reports the column sorted by and its direction, for tests and for
272	// views that show it elsewhere. Column is -1 when nothing is sorted.
273	func (m *Model[T]) SortState() (column int, desc bool) { return m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc }
274	
275	// Update handles the keys every table shares: navigation, `/` for the search,
276	// `.` for the sort, and whatever the filter bar takes while it is focused.
277	// Anything else is left alone, so the view keeps its own actions.
278	func (m *Model[T]) Update(msg tea.Msg) tea.Cmd {
279		if m.bar.InEditMode() {
280			var cmd tea.Cmd
281			m.bar, cmd = m.bar.Update(msg)
282			m.rebuild()
283			return cmd
284		}
285	
286		key, ok := msg.(tea.KeyMsg)
287		if !ok {
288			return nil
289		}
290		switch key.String() {
291		case "/":
292			// A table with nothing to search does not claim the key: activating a
293			// search that can only ever match nothing would empty the list, and the
294			// bar the user needs to see why is not in that view's footer.
295			if !m.Searchable() {
296				return nil
297			}
298			return m.bar.ActivateSearch()
299		case ".":
300			m.CycleSort()
301		case "up", "k":
302			m.table.MoveUp(1)
303			m.applyStyles()
304		case "down", "j":
305			m.table.MoveDown(1)
306			m.applyStyles()
307		case "pgup":
308			m.table.MoveUp(m.table.Height())
309			m.applyStyles()
310		case "pgdown":
311			m.table.MoveDown(m.table.Height())
312			m.applyStyles()
313		case "g", "home":
314			m.table.GotoTop()
315			m.applyStyles()
316		case "G", "end":
317			m.table.GotoBottom()
318			m.applyStyles()
319		}
320		return nil
321	}
322	
323	// SetTokenActive toggles one of the bar's filter tokens and re-applies it.
324	func (m *Model[T]) SetTokenActive(label string, active bool) {
325		m.bar.SetTokenActive(label, active)
326		m.rebuild()
327	}
328	
329	// IsTokenActive reports whether a toggle filter is on.
330	func (m *Model[T]) IsTokenActive(label string) bool { return m.bar.IsTokenActive(label) }
331	
332	// rebuild filters, sorts, writes the rows and puts the cursor somewhere real.
333	func (m *Model[T]) rebuild() {
334		m.visible = m.sorted(m.filtered())
335	
336		rows := make([]table.Row, len(m.visible))
337		for i, item := range m.visible {
338			cells := make(table.Row, len(m.cfg.Columns))
339			for j, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
340				cells[j] = c.Cell(item)
341			}
342			rows[i] = cells
343		}
344		m.table.SetRows(rows)
345	
346		// bubbles/table leaves the cursor where it was, so a list that just got
347		// shorter strands it past the end until the user presses a key. It also
348		// reports -1 while there are no rows at all, and that has to be taken back
349		// when rows return — a filter typed past its last match and then corrected
350		// would otherwise leave the table showing rows none of which is selected.
351		switch cursor := m.table.Cursor(); {
352		case len(rows) == 0:
353		case cursor >= len(rows):
354			m.table.SetCursor(len(rows) - 1)
355		case cursor < 0:
356			m.table.SetCursor(0)
357		}
358		m.applyStyles()
359	}
360	
361	// applyStyles asks the view for the styles that go with the selected item.
362	func (m *Model[T]) applyStyles() {
363		if !m.table.Focused() {
364			return // Blur owns the styles until Focus takes them back
365		}
366		styles := theme.DefaultTableStyles()
367		if item, ok := m.Selected(); ok && m.cfg.SelectedStyles != nil {
368			styles = m.cfg.SelectedStyles(item)
369		}
370		m.table.SetStyles(styles)
371	}
372	
373	// filtered applies the search query and the toggle filters.
374	func (m *Model[T]) filtered() []T {
375		query := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(m.bar.SearchQuery()))
376		active := m.activeTokens()
377	
378		out := make([]T, 0, len(m.items))
379		for _, item := range m.items {
380			if m.cfg.TokenMatch != nil && !m.cfg.TokenMatch(item, active) {
381				continue
382			}
383			if query != "" && !m.matchesQuery(item, query) {
384				continue
385			}
386			out = append(out, item)
387		}
388		return out
389	}
390	
391	func (m *Model[T]) activeTokens() map[string]bool {
392		active := make(map[string]bool, len(m.cfg.Tokens))
393		for _, tok := range m.cfg.Tokens {
394			if m.bar.IsTokenActive(tok.Label) {
395				active[tok.Label] = true
396			}
397		}
398		return active
399	}
400	
401	// matchesQuery tests the query against each searchable column and then against
402	// the row as a whole.
403	//
404	// The row-level pass is what keeps a query spanning two fields — "tcp 22" over a
405	// ports list — working: netdiag matched against a joined haystack while the
406	// other four filter loops matched per field, and per field alone would have
407	// quietly dropped those matches on migration. Matching both ways is a superset
408	// of either, so no view loses anything and they all gain the same thing.
409	func (m *Model[T]) matchesQuery(item T, query string) bool {
410		var joined strings.Builder
411		for _, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
412			if c.Search == nil {
413				continue
414			}
415			value := c.Search(item)
416			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value), query) {
417				return true
418			}
419			if joined.Len() > 0 {
420				joined.WriteByte(' ')
421			}
422			joined.WriteString(value)
423		}
424		return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(joined.String()), query)
425	}
426	
427	// sorted orders the visible slice. SliceStable, because sort.Slice is not and
428	// two rows equal on the sort column would otherwise swap between rebuilds.
429	func (m *Model[T]) sorted(items []T) []T {
430		if m.sortColumn < 0 {
431			return items
432		}
433		less := m.cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].Less // never nil — see New
434		desc := m.sortDesc
435		sort.SliceStable(items, func(i, j int) bool {
436			if desc {
437				return less(items[j], items[i])
438			}
439			return less(items[i], items[j])
440		})
441		return items
442	}

351	// New creates a new OCI resources view
352	func New(cfg *config.Config) Model {
353		s := spinner.New()
354		s.Spinner = spinner.Dot
355		s.Style = theme.SpinnerStyle()
356	
357		imageColumns := []table.Column{
358			{Title: "ID", Width: 14},
359			{Title: "Name", Width: 30},
360			{Title: "Disk Usage", Width: 12},
361			{Title: "Content Size", Width: 14},
362			{Title: "C", Width: 4},
363			{Title: "H", Width: 4},
364			{Title: "M", Width: 4},
365			{Title: "L", Width: 4},
366			{Title: "Scanned", Width: 14},
367		}
368		it := table.New(
369			table.WithColumns(imageColumns),
370			table.WithFocused(true),
371			table.WithHeight(10),
372		)
373		it.SetStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
374	
375		nt := datatable.New(datatable.Config[docker.Network]{Columns: networkColumns(), SortColumn: -1})
376		nt.Blur()
377	
378		vt := datatable.New(datatable.Config[docker.Volume]{Columns: volumeColumns(), SortColumn: -1})
379		vt.Blur()
380	
381		regColumns := []table.Column{
382			{Title: "Alias", Width: 16},
383			{Title: "URL", Width: 30},
384			{Title: "Kind", Width: 10},
385			{Title: "Auth", Width: 12}, // holds "credentials"
386			{Title: "Logged", Width: 8},
387			{Title: "Members", Width: 16},
388		}
389		rt := table.New(
390			table.WithColumns(regColumns),
391			table.WithFocused(false),
392			table.WithHeight(10),
393		)
394		rt.SetStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
395	
396		return Model{
397			config:              cfg,
398			activeTab:           tabImages,
399			scanCache:           make(map[string]cache.ImageScanEntry),
400			scanningImages:      make(map[string]bool),
401			failedScans:         make(map[string]bool),
402			spinner:             s,
403			filterBar:           sharedcomponents.NewFilterBar(),
404			imageTable:          it,
405			networkTable:        nt,
406			volumeTable:         vt,
407			registryTable:       rt,
408			registries:          cfg.Registry.Registries,
409			registryLoginStatus: make(map[string]bool),
410			groupCache:          make(map[string]cache.RegistryGroupEntry),
411			refreshingGroups:    make(map[string]bool),
412			browserDeselected:   make(map[string]bool),
413			loading:             true,
414			loadingNets:         true,
415			loadingVols:         true,
416			sortColumn:          sortByName,
417			sortAsc:             true,
418		}
419	}

421	// NewForSelection creates an OCI images view in selection mode for picking an image
422	func NewForSelection(cfg *config.Config, message string) Model {
423		m := New(cfg)
424		m.selectionMode = true
425		m.selectionMessage = message
426		return m
427	}

9	// handleImagesKeyMsg handles keys on the Images tab
10	func (m Model) handleImagesKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
11		switch msg.String() {
12		case "/":
13			return m, m.filterBar.ActivateSearch()
14		case "b":
15			return m.openMultiRegistryBrowser()
16		case "enter":
17			img := m.getSelectedImage()
18			if img == nil {
19				return m, nil
20			}
21			name := img.Name()
22			return m, func() tea.Msg { return ScanDetailsRequestMsg{ImageName: name} }
23		case "ctrl+e":
24			if m.isSelectedImageScanning() {
25				return m, nil
26			}
27			return m.openLaunchForm()
28		case "ctrl+d":
29			if m.isSelectedImageScanning() {
30				return m, nil
31			}
32			return m.deleteSelectedImage()
33		case "p":
34			return m.pruneImages()
35		case "ctrl+s":
36			if m.isSelectedImageScanning() {
37				return m, nil
38			}
39			return m.scanSelectedImage()
40		case "A":
41			return m.scanAllUnscanned()
42		case "ctrl+a":
43			return m.requestScanAll()
44		case ".":
45			return m.cycleSort()
46		case "ctrl+r":
47			m.loading = true
48			return m, tea.Batch(m.spinner.Tick, fetchImages(), loadScanCache())
49		case "up", "k":
50			m.imageTable.MoveUp(1)
51			return m, nil
52		case "down", "j":
53			m.imageTable.MoveDown(1)
54			return m, nil
55		case "g", "home":
56			m.imageTable.GotoTop()
57			return m, nil
58		case "G", "end":
59			m.imageTable.GotoBottom()
60			return m, nil
61		}
62		return m, nil
63	}

86		}

89		return m, cmd

169		switch msg.String() {

171			// A member is discovered, not declared, so there is nothing to add here.
172			if m.registryGroupSlug != "" {
173				return m, nil
174			}
175			m.registryForm = NewRegistryForm(m.registries, m.width-2)
176			return m, nil
177		case "e":
178			return m.editSelectedRegistry()
179		case "l":
180			return m.loginSelectedRegistry()
181		case "L":
182			return m.logoutSelectedRegistry()
183		case "ctrl+d":
184			return m.deleteSelectedRegistry()
185		case "ctrl+r":
186			return m.refreshRegistries()
187		// Rule 111 offers `l`/`h` as aliases for →/←, but `l` is login on this tab

189		case "right":
190			return m.enterSelectedGroup()
191		case "left", "esc":

193		case "up", "k":

207	}

`ports_model.go` lost 290 lines and gained the config.

`TestScrollSurvivesTheTwoSecondRefresh` is the one that matters, and it was
confirmed to bite by adding a `GotoTop` after `SetItems`: `cursor = 0 after a
refresh, want it left at 2`.

Two things this view forced into the component:

- **A row-level search pass.** netdiag matched a query against all six fields
  joined; the other four filter loops matched per field. Per field alone would
  have quietly dropped `"tcp 22"`-shaped matches on migration, so
  `matchesQuery` now tries each column *and* the joined row. That is a superset
  of either behaviour, so no view loses matches and the other five gain the same
  thing when they migrate.
- **`TokenMatch` got its first real client.** The proto and state groups are OR
  within a group and AND between them, and `numeric` / `paused` are tokens that
  report a mode rather than filtering. `matchesActive` makes the distinction
  that matters: a group with nothing on does not filter at all, which is not the
  same as matching nothing.

`internal/ui/netdiag` is at 85.6 %; the project total moved 81.9 % → 81.8 %,
the difference being the component's statements now counted against a view that
no longer has its own.

Étape 4 livrée — **PR #37**, CI verte (lint/build + tests, dont `test-race`).

## Ce qui a été fait

Deux commits, un par table.

**`containers`** — la première table à exercer `SelectedStyles`, le champ dont la conception avait été tranchée à l'étape 1 sans qu'aucun code de production ne s'en serve. C'est la seule des quinze dont la couleur de sélection dépend de la ligne (`exited`/`dead` → rouge). `refreshSelectionStyle` rejouait filtre-puis-tri **à chaque déplacement du curseur** pour savoir sur quoi il était ; c'est maintenant quatre lignes qui prennent un `docker.Container` et rendent des `table.Styles`.

**`oci_resources` images** — la table affiche ce que l'image n'est pas : le cache de scan, l'état du scan en cours, le nom substitué par alias. Les colonnes sont construites une fois dans `New` et ne peuvent rien atteindre de tout ça, donc `imageRow` porte la décoration. C'est ce qui rend la colonne `C` triable par le nombre qu'elle imprime — l'ancien comparateur allait rechercher l'entrée une seconde fois.

**Sorti des deux vues** : deux énumérations `sortField`, deux `sortableColumns`, deux `cycleSort`, deux blocs de flèches (deux maps et une boucle réécrivant dix en-têtes chacun), dix-sept cas de comparaison, deux boucles de filtre, les deux `getSelectedX`, quatre calculs de largeur, et la slice `containers`.

## Trois choses que la migration a fait remonter

**Le calcul de largeur des images pouvait passer négatif.** Il clampait Name à 20 puis donnait tout le déficit à Scanned — `available - 76` sous ce clamp, soit **-6 à 90 colonnes**. La *somme* Rule 116 restait exacte, et c'est précisément pour ça que rien ne l'attrapait : le total tombe juste pendant qu'une colonne est négative. Le test balaie depuis 60 maintenant et vérifie chaque colonne, pas seulement le total.

**L'état n'est pas une colonne** dans containers — c'est l'icône préfixée à l'image — mais le filtre l'a toujours matché. Même forme que la passe ligne-entière de l'étape 3 : la migration est le moment où un comportement sans colonne à lui se fait remarquer, et une recherche par colonne seule l'aurait perdu en silence.

**Le curseur est clampé** quand un filtre raccourcit la liste. `TestSelectionResolvesThroughSortAndFilter` n'a plus besoin de son `SetCursor` — cet appel *était* le bug, écrit dans le test.

Vérifié que ça mord dans les deux sens : `at width 60 the columns total 35, want 38` et `filtering on "prod" left []`.

## État du refactor

| | Étape | |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ | 1–3 | composant, networks+volumes, netdiag ports |
| ✅ | 4 | containers, images |
| ⬜ | 5 | workspaces, explorer — clamp et drill-down |
| ⬜ | 6 | security, status — les deux cas particuliers |

**5 tables sur 15.** Couverture : `containers` 84.9 %, `oci_resources` 76.1 %.

Reste à merger la #37 — dis-moi quand.

fix: resolve the workspaces selection against the rows on screen (D24)

The rows were filtered; m.entries was not. Every action resolved the
cursor against m.entries, so with a filter active they acted on whatever
sat at that index in the *unfiltered* list. Filtering five entries down
to "empty-dir" and pressing ctrl+d asked to delete "devdesk".

TestAFilteredSelectionActsOnTheRowTheUserSees was written first and
failed on the old code with "the confirmation does not name empty-dir".

The fix is the migration: datatable resolves a cursor against the very
slice its rows were built from, so the two cannot part. selectedIdx
becomes pendingEntry — a row index meant nothing once the list it
indexed stopped being the list on screen, and the modal that read it
back was the second place the two could disagree.

Also moved onto datatable in the same change (§2 step 5a):
- calculateColumns, which clamped Modified back up to 15 after handing
  it the remainder, so the columns overflowed by up to 34 at width 120.
  TestColumnsFitEveryWidth sweeps 80-220 and checks each column.
- the local cursor clamp, the filter loop, the row builder, and seven
  copies of the resolve-cursor-then-index block.
- workspaceRow carries the six scan cells, which depend on the cache,
  what is scanning and the spinner frame — same shape as imageRow.

datatable gained two things the view needed and every table wants:
- SetCursor, clamped. Workspaces restores a position per directory level
  on the way back up.
- The selected row is pinned to the content width. Column widths count
  cells, and a Nerd Font icon does not always render as wide as it
  counts, so the highlight stopped short of the border by whatever the
  icons disagreed by. It is a no-op when they agree.
- rebuild now sets the cursor to -1 on an empty list rather than leaving
  the old index, so an empty list stops being the one state where the
  cursor points past the end.

workspaces 81.7%, datatable 96.2%.
EOF

13	)
14	
15	// sortField defines which column to sort by
16	type sortField int
17	
18	const (
19		sortByType sortField = iota
20		sortByName
21		sortByVisibility
22		sortByCreated
23		sortByActivity
24	)
25	
26	// sortableColumns lists columns in cycle order for the '.' key
27	var sortableColumns = []sortField{
28		sortByType,
29		sortByName,
30		sortByVisibility,
31		sortByCreated,
32		sortByActivity,
33	}
34	
35	// ViewMode represents the current mode of the view
36	type ViewMode int
37	
38	const (
39		ModeNormal ViewMode = iota
40		ModePulling
41		ModeShowingReport
42		ModeLoadingTemplates
43		ModeCreatingProject
44		ModeConfirmingDelete
45	)
46	
47	// Model représente le modèle de la vue GitLab Explorer
48	type Model struct {
49		config *config.Config
50		shared *shared.State
51		width  int
52		height int
53	
54		// Table
55		table   table.Model
56		spinner spinner.Model
57	
58		// Tree state
59		nodes         []*TreeNode
60		loading       bool
61		firstLoadDone bool // true after the first load attempt completes (success or error)
62		error         string
63	
64		// Drill-down navigation
65		currentGroupNode *TreeNode   // nil = root level
66		navigationStack  []*TreeNode // Stack of parent groups for backspace navigation
67		cursorStack      []int       // Cursor positions per level for restoration on drill-up
68	
69		// Pull mode state
70		mode           ViewMode
71		reportModal    *components.ReportModal
72		pullTargetNode *TreeNode
73		pullStatus     string
74	
75		// Creation mode state
76		creationForm       *components.CreationForm
77		creationParentName string              // Parent stashed during template loading
78		creationParentID   int64               // Parent ID stashed during template loading
79		templateEntries    []oci.TemplateEntry // Loaded template entries for repo+tag resolution
80	
81		// Tab navigation
82		activeTabIndex int // Focused tab index (last tab = current level)
83	
84		// Delete mode state
85		deleteConfirmModal *components.DeleteConfirmModal
86		deleteTargetNode   *TreeNode
87		footerError        string // transient action error shown in footer (Rule 128)
88	
89		// Sorting
90		sortColumn sortField
91		sortAsc    bool
92	
93		// filterBar provides text search for the table (Rule 136)
94		filterBar components.FilterBar
95	
96		// Path to select after refresh (for newly created items)
97		pendingSelectPath string
98	}
99	
100	// New crée une nouvelle instance du modèle explorer
101	func New(cfg *config.Config, sharedState *shared.State) Model {
102		columns := []table.Column{
103			{Title: "Type", Width: 10},
104			{Title: "Name", Width: 25},
105			{Title: "Slug", Width: 20},
106			{Title: "Visibility", Width: 12},
107			{Title: "Role", Width: 12},
108			{Title: "Created", Width: 14},
109			{Title: "Activity", Width: 14},
110			{Title: "CI", Width: 10},
111		}
112	
113		t := table.New(
114			table.WithColumns(columns),
115			table.WithFocused(true),
116			table.WithHeight(10),
117		)
118		t.SetStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
119	
120		s := spinner.New()
121		s.Spinner = spinner.Dot
122		s.Style = theme.SpinnerStyle()
123	
124		return Model{
125			config:     cfg,
126			shared:     sharedState,
127			nodes:      []*TreeNode{},
128			loading:    false,
129			mode:       ModeNormal,
130			table:      t,

132			sortColumn: sortByType,
133			sortAsc:    true,
134			filterBar:  components.NewFilterBar(),
135		}
136	}

138	// Init initialise le modèle
139	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
140		// Charger les groupes racine au démarrage
141		if m.shared.GitLabClient != nil {
142			m.loading = true
143			return tea.Batch(m.spinner.Tick, m.loadRootGroups())
144		}
145		return nil
146	}
147	
148	// InEditMode returns true if the view is in an edit mode or filter search
149	func (m Model) InEditMode() bool {
150		return m.creationForm != nil || m.mode != ModeNormal || m.filterBar.InEditMode()
151	}
152	
153	// FilterBarVisible returns true when the filter bar is visible (implements app.FilterBarView).
154	func (m Model) FilterBarVisible() bool {
155		if !m.filterBar.IsVisible() || m.loading || m.error != "" || len(m.nodes) == 0 {
156			return false
157		}
158		switch m.mode {
159		case ModePulling, ModeLoadingTemplates, ModeCreatingProject, ModeConfirmingDelete, ModeShowingReport:
160			return false
161		}
162		return m.creationForm == nil
163	}
164	
165	// tabCount returns the total number of tabs (home + navigation stack + current group)
166	func (m Model) tabCount() int {
167		count := 1 // home tab
168		for _, node := range m.navigationStack {
169			if node != nil {
170				count++
171			}
172		}
173		if m.currentGroupNode != nil {
174			count++
175		}
176		return count
177	}
178	
179	// resize adjusts table dimensions based on terminal size
180	func (m *Model) resize(width, height int) {
181		m.filterBar.Resize(width)
182		// Rule 124: footer (tab bar + filter bar) is outside the viewport; subtract table header only
183		tableDataHeight := height - 1
184		if tableDataHeight < 1 {
185			tableDataHeight = 1
186		}
187		m.table.SetHeight(tableDataHeight)
188	
189		// Column widths (Rule 116: contentWidth = width - 2, available = contentWidth - numColumns*2)
190		contentWidth := width - 2

content.text:
#37 mergée. **PR #38** ouverte pour l'étape 5, CI verte.

## L'étape 5 a trouvé un défaut de perte de données — D24

`workspaces` filtrait les lignes mais pas `m.entries`, et **sept copies** du même bloc transformaient un curseur *dans les lignes* en index *dans une autre liste* :

```go
idx := m.table.Cursor()
if idx < 0 || idx >= len(m.entries) { return m, nil }
entry := m.entries[idx]
```

Filtre cinq entrées jusqu'à `empty-dir`, `ctrl+d` → la confirmation dit **devdesk**. `ctrl+s`, `r`, `enter`, `ctrl+o`, `ctrl+w` étaient faux de la même façon.

C'est exactement la classe de défaut pour laquelle la doc de package de `datatable` a été écrite — *« si elles divergent, l'action atterrit sur le mauvais objet et ne dit rien »*. Elle était vivante dans la seule vue où la conséquence est un répertoire supprimé.

Test écrit avant le correctif, échoue sur l'ancien code : `the confirmation does not name empty-dir`.

`selectedIdx` est parti avec : la modale qui le relisait après confirmation était le second endroit où les deux listes pouvaient diverger.

## L'explorer en avait deux de la même famille

`expandToPath` parcourait `currentItems()` — sous un tri non-défaut, un ordre différent des lignes, et **les deux index dans les bornes**, donc rien ne masquait l'erreur par clamp. Confirmé : `cursor is on "sub", want legacy`.

Et quatre handlers gardaient avec `cursor >= len(items)`, ce qui laisse passer le `-1` de bubbles : `ctrl+d` sur un groupe vide indexait `[-1]`.

## Les deux calculs de largeur étaient faux, en sens opposés

`workspaces` re-clampait Modified à 15 **après** lui avoir donné le reste → débordement jusqu'à 34 colonnes. L'explorer gardait la somme exacte et affamait les colonnes : à 80, Type avait 5 et Created 8, ni l'un ni l'autre assez large pour son propre en-tête.

**Une somme correcte n'est pas une mise en page correcte**, et une seule des deux est ce que dit vraiment la Rule 116.

## Ce que les vues ont imposé au composant

`SetCursor` clampé, la ligne sélectionnée épinglée à la largeur du contenu (workspaces le faisait à la main — bon instinct : une icône Nerd Font ne s'affiche pas toujours aussi large qu'elle compte), et le curseur à `-1` sur liste vide.

refactor: move the security findings table onto datatable (§2 step 6a)

The second client of SelectedStyles, and the special case the backlog
called out: this view filters by tab and severity *before* any query, and
resets the cursor to the top when the tab changes — the opposite of what
SetItems does by default.

Both stay in the view, which is right. The tab and the severity select
which findings exist at all; a FilterBar query narrows a list that is
already settled. So the view filters and hands the result over, and calls
GotoTop explicitly — the call SetItems deliberately does not make.

What left the view: refreshSelectionStyle and its bounds check,
calculateColumns, getTitleColumnWidth, filteredFindings, and the
resolve-cursor-then-index blocks in handleIgnoreSecret and enter.

Two things the migration turned up:

- The Title was truncated by hand at width-3 before being put in the row.
  bubbles truncates every cell to its column width with the same ellipsis
  (table.go:429), so this only cost three characters of title.
- Nothing depends on the width when building rows any more, so the
  resize handler stopped rebuilding them — and NewWithPreloadedResult
  stopped relying on a WindowSizeMsg to fill its table. It fills it.

selectedIdx becomes selectedFinding. The details view is about a finding,
not about a row index, and an index names a different one the moment the
list changes under it — which is how workspaces got D24.

TestColumnsFitTheWidth looped over three widths and `continue`d when the
sum was wrong, so it asserted nothing. It sweeps from 50 now and checks
each column.

security 85.4%.

'''**D25 — status acted on the wrong monitor under a filter. Fixed** by §2 step 6,
which is also what found it. `getSelectedComponentIndex` replayed the sort by
hand and then indexed, but never applied the text filter the rows had already
been through; the SSL branch walked `m.components` by counting, unfiltered the
same way. Under a filter `e` edited and `ctrl+d` deleted a monitor the user was
not looking at. Same family as D24, and the ninth and last copy of the block.
`TestAFilteredSelectionEditsTheRowTheUserSees` was written before the fix and
failed on the old code.

**D24 — workspaces acted on the wrong directory under a filter. Fixed** by §2''')

step6 = '''
#### Step 6 as built — `security`, then `status`

The two the plan set aside as not fitting the config cleanly. Both turned out to
fit — by keeping something the component deliberately does not model.

**`security`** filters by tab and by severity before any query, and resets the
cursor to the top when the tab changes. Both stay in the view, and that is the
right answer rather than a concession: the tab and the severity decide which
findings *exist*, where a `FilterBar` query narrows a list that is already
settled. So the view filters and hands the result over, then calls `GotoTop`
explicitly — the call `SetItems` deliberately does not make. It is the second
client of `SelectedStyles`, colouring the selected row by the severity under the
cursor.

**`status`** is two tables sharing a viewport with alternating focus, and it is
two `datatable.Model` plus a four-line `applyTabFocus`, exactly as the plan
guessed. `Focus` and `Blur` carry the styles, so the four `SetStyles` calls at
every tab switch went with them. The one text query drives *both* tables so the
header counts agree with each other whichever tab is showing, so the query stays
in the view too — same call as security's, for the same reason.

**And status was carrying D25.** `getSelectedComponentIndex` sorted and then
indexed without ever applying the filter the rows had been through. It is the
ninth and last copy of the block, and the second of the nine that was actually
wrong. Two out of nine is the answer to whether this refactor was worth doing on
correctness grounds: the duplication was not equivalent, it had drifted, and
nothing said so.

Two smaller things:

- The findings Title was truncated by hand at `width-3` before going into the
  row. bubbles truncates every cell to its column width with the same ellipsis
  (`table.go:429`), so this only ever cost three characters of title. Nothing
  else depended on the width when building rows, so the resize handler stopped
  rebuilding them — and `NewWithPreloadedResult` stopped needing a
  `WindowSizeMsg` to fill its table.
- `matchesQuery` settles an inconsistency nobody chose: status' monitor loop
  matched name, target and type; the SSL loop left type out.

`security` 85.5 %, `status` 93.1 %.

#### §2 done — fifteen of fifteen

What it removed, across the six steps: twelve width calculations (five of them
wrong — three that overflowed, two that starved), nine `getSelectedX` (two of

content.text:
#38 mergée. **PR #39** ouverte — CI verte. **Le refactor est terminé : 15 tables sur 15.**

## D25 — status agissait sur le mauvais moniteur sous filtre

`getSelectedComponentIndex` rejouait le tri à la main puis indexait — **sans jamais appliquer le filtre texte** que les lignes avaient déjà subi. La branche SSL parcourait `m.components` en comptant, non filtrée pareil. Sous filtre, `e` éditait et `ctrl+d` supprimait un moniteur que l'utilisateur ne regardait pas.

Même famille que D24, et **la neuvième et dernière copie** du bloc résoudre-le-curseur-puis-indexer.

**Deux des neuf copies étaient réellement fausses.** C'est la réponse à la question de savoir si ce refactor valait le coup sur des bases de correction : la duplication n'était pas équivalente, elle avait dérivé, et rien ne le disait.

## Les deux cas particuliers rentrent — en gardant ce que le composant ne modélise pas

**`security`** : l'onglet et la sévérité décident quelles findings *existent* ; une requête FilterBar rétrécit une liste déjà arrêtée. La vue filtre, passe le résultat, et appelle `GotoTop` explicitement — le reset que `SetItems` ne fait délibérément pas.

**`status`** : deux `datatable.Model` plus un `applyTabFocus` de quatre lignes, exactement comme le plan l'avait deviné. `Focus`/`Blur` emportent les styles, donc les quatre `SetStyles` à chaque changement d'onglet sont partis.

Trouvailles secondaires : le Titre des findings était tronqué à la main à `width-3` alors que bubbles tronque déjà chaque cellule à sa largeur avec la même ellipse (`table.go:429`) — ça coûtait trois caractères pour rien. Et `TestColumnsFitTheWidth` bouclait sur trois largeurs en faisant `continue` quand la somme était fausse : il n'assertait **rien**.

## Bilan des six étapes

Retiré : 12 calculs de largeur (5 faux — 3 qui débordaient, 2 qui affamaient), 9 `getSelectedX` (2 faux), 8 blocs de flèches de tri, 6 énumérations `sortField` avec leur `cycleSort`, 11 boucles de filtre, et le trio `tableReady`.

Le but n'a jamais été le nombre de lignes — ~1500 sorties des vues contre 560 dans le composant et ses tests. C'est que les Rules 116, 122 et 136 ont cessé d'être des conventions vérifiées en revue.

Les deux défauts trouvés avaient la même forme, et aucun n'était théorique : filtrer une liste, agir sur la ligne surlignée, regarder le mauvais objet disparaître.

## Reste au backlog

- **§3.6** multiforge GitHub/GitLab — sketch en 8 étapes, dont deux autonomes
- **§3.1–3.5, §3.10** — non démarrées
- **D21** — seul défaut ouvert, trois lignes de code mort
- **§4** — plan de portabilité Docker

Dis-moi quand merger la #39.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   All requests were in French, in the DevDesk repo (`C:\Users\anthoni\projects\entire\anthnel\devdesk`), a Go + Bubble Tea TUI. This session was a continuous march through the §2 table refactor in `docs/backlog.md`:

   - **"continue le refactor, point 4"** (with a table showing steps 1–3 ✅ and 4–6 ⬜) — do step 4: `containers`, then `oci_resources` images.
   - **"merge et continue"** (×2) — merge the open PR and move to the next step (5, then 6).
   - **"merge"** — merge PR #39.

   Standing constraints (from CLAUDE.md and memory, still in force):
   - **Never push directly to `main`** — the Entire mirror rejects it (`! [remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch)`). Use branch + PR: `git switch -c <branch>`, `git push origin <branch>`, `gh pr create --base main`, `gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch`, `git fetch origin && git merge --ff-only origin/main`.
   - **Never delete or touch `entire/*` git branches** — that is where Entire stores session context.
   - **No secret goes in the config file.** `GitLabConfig` has no `Token`, `RegistryConfig` has no `Password`; both live in the host secret store. Do not add a secret-bearing field back — the schema is what makes the guarantee checkable.
   - Tests must redirect `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` so they never rewrite the developer's own `~/.devdesk`.
   - `golangci-lint run` / `mise run lint` is mandatory before commits (Rules 301–306).
   - `mise run test-race` needs cgo/gcc which is absent locally; CI runs it on every PR.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - Go 1.25 generics, Bubble Tea (Elm architecture), `bubbles/table`, `bubbles/textinput`, `bubbles/spinner`, lipgloss
   - Project rules: 110 (never mutate model in a Cmd), 111 (standard keybindings incl. `.` sort, `/` filter, pgup/pgdown), 112, 114, 116 (column widths sum to available), 118 (table/tab colours), 122 (no `style.Render()` in `table.Row` — ANSI bleeds), 123, 124 (layout/footer heights), 126, 127 (`theme.TimeAgo`), 128, 129 (English US UI/logs), 130 (dynamic shortcuts), 132, 135, 136 (FilterBar), 201, 301–306
   - **Row types** (`imageRow`, `workspaceRow`) carrying decoration that doesn't live on the domain object, because columns are built once in `New` and can't reach the model
   - **Writing the defect test first** and confirming it fails on the old code (D24, D25)
   - **Verifying a test bites**: temporarily break the fix, confirm the exact failure message, restore
   - `bubbles/table` truncates every cell with `runewidth.Truncate(value, width, "…")` at `table.go:429` — hand-truncation is redundant
   - `bubbles/table` `SetCursor` clamps via `clamp(v, 0, len-1)`, which yields `-1` on an empty table

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   **`internal/ui/datatable/datatable.go`** — the shared component; gained three things this session:
   ```go
   // SetCursor puts the cursor on a row, clamped to what exists. Views that
   // remember a position across a reload — workspaces restores one per directory
   // level on the way back up — call this; nothing else should need it.
   func (m *Model[T]) SetCursor(i int) {
       if len(m.visible) == 0 { return }
       m.table.SetCursor(min(max(i, 0), len(m.visible)-1))
       m.applyStyles()
   }
   ```
   ```go
   func (m *Model[T]) applyStyles() {
       if !m.table.Focused() { return }
       styles := theme.DefaultTableStyles()
       if item, ok := m.Selected(); ok && m.cfg.SelectedStyles != nil {
           styles = m.cfg.SelectedStyles(item)
       }
       // Pin the selected row to the full content width. Column widths are counted
       // in cells, and a Nerd Font icon does not always render as wide as it
       // counts, so the highlight otherwise stops short of the right border...
       if m.width > 2 { styles.Selected = styles.Selected.Width(m.width - 2) }
       m.table.SetStyles(styles)
   }
   ```
   ```go
   switch cursor := m.table.Cursor(); {
   case len(rows) == 0:
       // -1 is bubbles' own "nothing selected"...
       m.table.SetCursor(-1)
   case cursor >= len(rows): m.table.SetCursor(len(rows) - 1)
   case cursor < 0: m.table.SetCursor(0)
   }
   ```
   `Resize` now ends with `m.applyStyles() // the selected row is pinned to this width`.

   **`internal/ui/containers/model.go`** — `columnName/columnImage/columnPorts` consts, `containerColumns()` (10 columns; Image `Search` returns `c.Image + " " + c.State`), `containerSelectedStyles(c) table.Styles` (exited/dead → error), `New` builds `datatable.New(datatable.Config[docker.Container]{Columns: containerColumns(), SortColumn: columnName, SelectedStyles: containerSelectedStyles})`.

   **`internal/ui/containers/update.go`** — metrics merge now clones:
   ```go
   containers := slices.Clone(m.containerTable.Items())
   for i, c := range containers { if metrics, ok := msg.Metrics[c.ID]; ok { ... } }
   m.containerTable.SetItems(containers)
   ```
   Navigation collapsed to `case "up","k","down","j","pgup","pgdown","g","home","G","end","/",".": return m, m.containerTable.Update(msg)`. `resize` is `m.containerTable.Resize(width, height-2)`.

   **`internal/ui/oci_resources/table.go`** — `imageRow{Image, DisplayName, RawName, Entry, Scanned, Scanning, Failed, SpinnerFrame}`, `imageColumnName = 1`, `cveColumn(title, get)`, `scannedCell(r)`, `imageColumns()`, `imageRows()`. `updateImageTable()` is now `m.imageTable.SetItems(m.imageRows()); m.imageTable.SetHeight(m.tableHeight())`. Name column `Search: func(r imageRow) string { return r.DisplayName + " " + r.RawName }`.

   **`internal/ui/workspaces/columns.go`** (new) — width consts, `numColumns = 11`, `workspaceRow{Entry, Sensitive, Critical, High, Medium, Low, Scanned}`, `workspaceColumns()`, `rowsFor(entries)`.

   **`internal/ui/workspaces/table.go`** — now holds `updateTableSize` (one `m.table.Resize(m.width, max(m.height-1, 1))`), `setEntries`, `refreshRows`, `entries()`, and:
   ```go
   // selectedEntry returns the entry under the cursor.
   //
   // Every action used to index the *unfiltered* list with a cursor into the
   // filtered rows... and ctrl+d asked to delete it (D24).
   func (m Model) selectedEntry() (Entry, bool) {
       row, ok := m.table.Selected()

   }
   ```

   **`internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/columns.go`** (new) — `numColumns = 8`, min-width consts, `columnType = 0`, `explorerColumns()` (Slug's `Search` returns `n.FullPath`), `timeBefore()`. `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/table.go` was **deleted**; `updateTableRows()` moved to `navigation.go` as `m.table.SetItems(m.currentItems())`.

   **`internal/ui/security/findings.go`** — `numColumns = 4`, `findingColumns()`, `findingSelectedStyles(f) table.Styles`, `sourceDisplay(f)` (free function). `updateFindingsTable` filters by tab+severity then `SetItems` + explicit `GotoTop()`.

   **`internal/ui/status/columns.go`** (new) — `numMonitorColumns = 5`, `numSSLColumns = 6`, `columnName = 0`, `monitorColumns()`, `monitorStatusCell()`, `monitorTypeCell()`, `sslColumns()`.

   **`internal/ui/status/view.go`** — `updateTable()` filters once with `matchesQuery` then `SetItems` on both tables, plus:
   ```go
   func matchesQuery(comp status.ComponentStatus, query string) bool {
       if query == "" { return true }
       return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(comp.Name), query) ||
           strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(comp.Target), query) ||
           strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(string(comp.Type)), query)
   }
   func (m *Model) applyTabFocus() {
       if m.activeTab == TabMonitors { m.monitorTable.Focus(); m.sslTable.Blur(); return }
       m.sslTable.Focus(); m.monitorTable.Blur()
   }
   ```

   **`internal/ui/status/update.go`** — `getSelectedComponentIndex` reduced to `Selected()` + a config lookup by name/type/target.

   **`docs/backlog.md`** and **`.claude/CLAUDE.md`** — updated after every step with "Step N as built" blocks, D24/D25 entries, and a closing "§2 done — fifteen of fifteen".

4. **Errors and fixes:**
   - **Bash heredoc parse failure** (`unexpected EOF while looking for matching ''`) → wrote Python scripts to the scratchpad (`ws1.py`…`st3.py`, `doc6.py`) and ran them by absolute path.

   - **`cannot call pointer method Table on datatable.Model[...]`** when chained off a function call → assign to a variable first (`m := drilledModel(t)`, `first := scannedModel(t)`).
   - **Stale LSP diagnostics** repeatedly reported already-fixed symbols as undefined; ignored when `go build` and `golangci-lint` were clean.
   - **golangci-lint `unused`**: `visibleItems` (explorer) and `findings` (security) → deleted both.
   - **golangci-lint S1021** in workspaces → collapsed `var cmd tea.Cmd; cmd = …; return m, cmd` to `return m, m.table.Update(msg)`.
   - **`TestCursorNeverPointsPastTheEnd` failed** (`cursor = 4 on an empty list`) → added `m.table.SetCursor(-1)` to `rebuild`'s empty case.
   - **`TestNewWithPreloadedResultOpensOnTheResults` failed** after removing the resize rebuild → `NewWithPreloadedResult` now calls `m.updateFindingsTable()` itself.
   - **The D24 test initially failed for the wrong reason** (`mode = 0 after ctrl+d`) because the filter bar still had focus → added `testutil.Key("enter")` to confirm the filter before acting.
   - **`doc6.py` raised "step 6 block not inserted"** because the anchor text had changed → re-pointed the replace at `tables migrated. Step 6 stands as written.`
   - **Missing imports** repeatedly (`datatable`, `cache`, `docker`, `strings`, `tea`) — fixed each time.
   - **No user feedback corrected my approach** in this session; all three follow-ups were "merge" / "merge et continue".

5. **Problem Solving:**

import io

p = 'docs/backlog.md'
s = io.open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()

s = s.replace('''**D24 — workspaces acted on the wrong directory under a filter. Fixed** by §2''',
'''**D25 — status acted on the wrong monitor under a filter. Fixed** by §2 step 6,
which is also what found it. `getSelectedComponentIndex` replayed the sort by
hand and then indexed, but never applied the text filter the rows had already
been through; the SSL branch walked `m.components` by counting, unfiltered the
same way. Under a filter `e` edited and `ctrl+d` deleted a monitor the user was
not looking at. Same family as D24, and the ninth and last copy of the block.
`TestAFilteredSelectionEditsTheRowTheUserSees` was written before the fix and
failed on the old code.

**D24 — workspaces acted on the wrong directory under a filter. Fixed** by §2''')

step6 = '''
#### Step 6 as built — `security`, then `status`

The two the plan set aside as not fitting the config cleanly. Both turned out to
fit — by keeping something the component deliberately does not model.

**`security`** filters by tab and by severity before any query, and resets the
cursor to the top when the tab changes. Both stay in the view, and that is the
right answer rather than a concession: the tab and the severity decide which
findings *exist*, where a `FilterBar` query narrows a list that is already
settled. So the view filters and hands the result over, then calls `GotoTop`
explicitly — the call `SetItems` deliberately does not make. It is the second
client of `SelectedStyles`, colouring the selected row by the severity under the
cursor.

**`status`** is two tables sharing a viewport with alternating focus, and it is
two `datatable.Model` plus a four-line `applyTabFocus`, exactly as the plan
guessed. `Focus` and `Blur` carry the styles, so the four `SetStyles` calls at
every tab switch went with them. The one text query drives *both* tables so the
header counts agree with each other whichever tab is showing, so the query stays
in the view too — same call as security's, for the same reason.

**And status was carrying D25.** `getSelectedComponentIndex` sorted and then
indexed without ever applying the filter the rows had been through. It is the
ninth and last copy of the block, and the second of the nine that was actually
wrong. Two out of nine is the answer to whether this refactor was worth doing on
correctness grounds: the duplication was not equivalent, it had drifted, and
nothing said so.

Two smaller things:

- The findings Title was truncated by hand at `width-3` before going into the
  row. bubbles truncates every cell to its column width with the same ellipsis
  (`table.go:429`), so this only ever cost three characters of title. Nothing
  else depended on the width when building rows, so the resize handler stopped
  rebuilding them — and `NewWithPreloadedResult` stopped needing a
  `WindowSizeMsg` to fill its table.
- `matchesQuery` settles an inconsistency nobody chose: status' monitor loop
  matched name, target and type; the SSL loop left type out.

`security` 85.5 %, `status` 93.1 %.

#### §2 done — fifteen of fifteen

What it removed, across the six steps: twelve width calculations (five of them
wrong — three that overflowed, two that starved), nine `getSelectedX` (two of
them wrong, D24 and D25), eight sort-arrow blocks, six `sortField` enums and
their `cycleSort`, eleven filter loops, and the `tableReady` trio.

What it bought is not the line count — roughly 1500 lines out of the views
against 560 in the component and its tests. It is that Rules 116, 122 and 136
stopped being conventions checked in review. `Cell func(T) string` gives styled
text nowhere to go. One solver makes the width invariant testable, and every
view now sweeps it from a width narrow enough to hurt. `SetItems` is the only
place a cursor can be left dangling, and `Selected()` reads the slice the rows
were built from, so the two cannot part.

Both defects it found were the same shape and neither was hypothetical: filter a
list, act on the highlighted row, watch the wrong object get deleted.

'''

s = s.replace('''tables migrated. Step 6 stands as written.
''', '''tables migrated.
''' + step6)

# the step-5 block ends with "Step 6 stands as written." already; make sure we replaced the right one
if '#### Step 6 as built' not in s:
    raise SystemExit("step 6 block not inserted")
io.open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='').write(s)

p = '.claude/CLAUDE.md'
s = io.open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
s = s.replace('''Migration of the fifteen existing tables is step-by-step: `oci_resources`
networks, volumes and images, `netdiag` ports, `containers`, `workspaces` and
the GitLab `explorer` are done — `security` and `status` are what is left. See
the backlog.''',
'''**All fifteen tables are migrated.** A new table uses `datatable`; there is no
second way to build one.

Two views keep a filter of their own, and deliberately. `security` selects
findings by tab and by severity, and `status` drives both its tables from one
search box so the header counts agree — in both cases the view filters and calls
`SetItems`, because a `FilterBar` query narrows a list that is already settled
and these decide which rows exist at all. `security` also calls `GotoTop`
explicitly on a tab change, which is the reset `SetItems` does not make.

`status` is the two-table case: two `datatable.Model` plus a focus helper.
`Focus` and `Blur` carry the styles with them (Rule 118), so a tab switch does
not touch `SetStyles`.''')

### 3.7 Command mode from inside a text field — **done**

`alt+:` now opens the command line from anywhere, including a focused text
input. A bare `:` keeps its old, conditional behaviour, so muscle memory
survives.

The problem: `handleKeyMsg` routed `:` through `maybeEnterInCommandMode`, which
asked the view whether it was in edit mode (`FormView.InEditMode()`) and, if it
was, forwarded the keystroke to the active input. Command mode was therefore
unreachable from any form, filter box or search field — most of the application.

The security view is the case that settles it. `InEditMode()` is true there for
the target path, Trivy server and Gitleaks config fields, and the Trivy server
placeholder is `https://trivy-server:4954` — the field has to accept **two**
colons to hold a valid value. Forwarding `:` to the input is not a bug; it is
the only correct behaviour, which is precisely why `:` cannot be the
authoritative key. The only way in was to move focus to a control that takes no
text and press `:` there, so reachability depended on which widget was focused
and nothing said so.

It was worse in `StateScanning`, `StateResults`, `StateDetails` and while a
confirm modal is open: `InEditMode()` is true and there is no field to move
focus to. `:` was forwarded to the view, which has no `case` for it — no view in
the application handles `:` itself — and dropped silently.

#### Why `alt+`, not `ctrl+`

`ctrl+:` cannot be made to work, and this is the note that should stop anyone
reintroducing it. A terminal encodes Ctrl by clearing bits, which only covers
ASCII `@` through `_` (0x40–0x5F). `:` is 0x3A: Ctrl+: sends a plain `:` or
nothing. Reporting it as a distinct key needs the Kitty keyboard protocol or
xterm's `modifyOtherKeys`, and bubbletea v1.3.10 implements neither. A
`case "ctrl+:"` would be dead code.

Alt has no such limit — a terminal sends ESC then the key, and bubbletea reports
that as the key carrying `Alt`. The alternative considered was a free
`ctrl+<letter>` (`b g l p t u v x z` are unused; `ctrl+i m j h [` are Tab, Enter,
LF, Backspace and Esc and must be left alone), which is marginally more portable
but loses the `:` in the gesture.

#### What shipped

- `altCommandModeKey` is handled in `handleKeyMsg` **before** the `InEditMode()`
  fork, so no view can claim it. The router sees every `tea.KeyMsg` first, which
  is what makes the binding unconditional.
- `enterCommandMode()` extracted; `maybeEnterInCommandMode` now only answers the
  bare `:`.
- `testutil.Key` understands an `alt+` prefix, building the key with the `Alt`
  modifier rather than the five literal runes `alt+:`. Both round-trip through
  `String()`, but only one is the message the application actually receives.
- Every `GetShortcuts()` and `GetHelpContent()` advertising `:` now advertises
  `alt+:` (Rules 114, 130, 137). The dashboard's Navigation help section carries
  the nuance in prose, so the other eight sites stay one line each.
- The header still renders `:` as the inactive prompt: it is the command line's
  visual marker, not a key legend, and `:` remains valid whenever no field has
  focus.

Two things the ripple list got wrong, corrected here: `app_test.go:30` is a
layout fixture for `buildShortcutLines`, not an assertion about the binding, so
it was left alone. And `CommandModeView` / `AllowCommandMode` was not merely
made redundant by this change — **it was already dead code**. The router only
consulted it when `InEditMode()` was true, and netdiag's implementation returns
true only on the topology tab, where `InEditMode()` is unconditionally false. It
could never fire. Deleted, along with its one implementation;
`TestCommandModeOnTheTopologyTab` became
`TestTheTopologyTabNeverBlocksCommandMode` and records why.

J'ai regardé le code avant de répondre, parce que ton intuition dépend de faits vérifiables et il y en a un qui la valide plus fort que tu ne le dis, et un autre qui la contredit.

## D'accord sur la moitié, et c'est la moitié que tu as raison de vouloir

**La vue config : oui, sans réserve.** Le schéma compte ~42 champs éditables. Aujourd'hui, atteignables depuis le TUI : le thème (`:theme`), les monitors (CRUD status), les registres (`RegistryForm`), l'URL GitLab (auth), et 9 options de scan. Soit ~13. Tout le reste s'édite à la main dans le YAML :

| Section | Hors d'atteinte |
|---|---|
| `app` | `workspaces_dir`, `ide_command`, `terminal_command`, `secret_backend`, `default_view`, `log_file` |
| `status` | `refresh_interval`, `timeout`, `auto_refresh` |
| `gitlab` | `default_parent_group`, `clone_method`, les 4 `pull.*` |
| `scan` | `trivy_image`, `gitleaks_image`, `max_concurrent_scans`, `timeout`, `sbom_output_dir`, les caches |
| `docker` | `network_tool_image` |

`secret_backend` est le cas qui tranche : c'est une décision de sécurité, documentée dans CLAUDE.md, avec trois valeurs et un fallback — et le seul moyen de la changer est d'ouvrir un fichier. C'est un champ à cycle `←→` qui n'existe pas.

## Pas d'accord sur l'autre moitié — mais pas pour la raison à laquelle tu t'attends

Le formulaire `security` n'est **qu'un état sur quatre** : `StateInput` → `StateScanning` → `StateResults` → `StateDetails`. Tu proposes de supprimer le premier. Les trois autres — la table de findings avec ses onglets CVE/Secrets/Licenses/Misconfig, le filtre de sévérité, le détail avec remédiation, le flow "ignore secret" — c'est l'outil. Ça ne va nulle part.

Et c'est là que ton intuition est **plus juste que ta formulation** : ce flow existe déjà.

```go
// internal/ui/workspaces/actions.go:143
func (m Model) getScanOptions() scan.ScanOptions { ... m.config.Scan.EnableVuln ... }

// internal/ui/oci_resources/images.go:79
func (m Model) defaultScanOpts() scan.ScanOptions { ... m.config.Scan.EnableVuln ... }
```

Deux copies **octet pour octet identiques**, qui lisent la config et pas le formulaire. `ctrl+s` sur une image ou sur un dépôt ne passe déjà plus par la vue `sec`. Et `NewWithPreloadedResult` ouvre déjà directement sur `StateResults`. Ce que tu décris est implémenté à 80 % ; ce qui reste est le formulaire, qui est devenu le seul chemin qui utilise *autre chose* que la config.

## Le défaut que ça révèle

Troisième constructeur, `security/scan.go:31`, et il n'est pas identique :

```go
IgnoreEOL:  m.ignoreEOL,   // ← seulement ici
```

`IgnoreEOL` est coché dans le formulaire, persisté dans `config.Scan.IgnoreEOL`, câblé jusqu'à `--ignore-status end_of_life` dans `scanner.go`. Et **les deux autres constructeurs ne le passent pas**. Tu coches "ignore EOL", tu scannes depuis la liste d'images, l'option est silencieusement ignorée. Trois copies, une divergente — exactement le motif de D24/D25 qu'on vient de fermer neuf fois dans les tables.

C'est l'argument décisif pour ta proposition, et il est meilleur que "meilleure UX" : **un seul constructeur alimenté par la config rend ce défaut impossible par construction.**

## Ce que je proposerais à la place de supprimer

Inverser la vue plutôt que la retirer. `:sec` cesse d'être « configurer et lancer », devient **l'inventaire de ce qui a été scanné** — les deux caches exposent déjà `GetAll()` :

```
:sec  →  table unifiée images + workspaces, triée par CRITICAL
         enter → StateResults (déjà écrit)
         ctrl+s → relance avec les options de la config
```

Tu y gagnes trois choses : `:sec` a enfin une page d'accueil qui a un sens (aujourd'hui c'est un formulaire vide), la question « qu'est-ce qui est cassé, tout périmètre confondu » trouve une réponse — rien ne la donne aujourd'hui —, et le formulaire disparaît quand même.

## Les trois questions qui décident du design

1. **La vue config absorbe-t-elle les CRUD existants, ou pointe-t-elle dessus ?** Les monitors ont un CRUD dans `status`, les registres ont `RegistryForm`. Les dupliquer serait le contraire de ce que tu cherches. Je pencherais pour : la config édite les scalaires, et les listes restent où elles sont éditées.
2. **Où vit `applyServerModeConstraints` ?** Renseigner un serveur Trivy force `misconfig`/`license`/`sbom` à false — le protocole client-serveur ne les supporte pas. C'est une contrainte inter-champs, pas un défaut ; elle doit suivre les champs dans la vue config.
3. **Que devient le picker de cible ?** `b` ouvre le browser de fichiers ou d'images. Si les scans partent des listes, il n'a plus d'appelant — mais c'est aussi le seul moyen de scanner un chemin arbitraire hors `workspaces_dir`. À trancher explicitement plutôt que par omission.

Un dernier point, ta règle et pas la mienne : le plan lui-même revient à Antigravity. Ce que je peux faire tout de suite sans empiéter, c'est fermer le défaut `IgnoreEOL` — il tient en une fonction partagée et il est vrai indépendamment de la suite.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**: 
> - Support for **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** only.
> - **Planning** and **Brainstorming** are handled by Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](file:///home/anthoni/projects/gitlab/devsecops/devdesk/project-context.md) for global project rules.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, clone/pull)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/misconfig/SBOM + Gitleaks secrets)
