input.content:
# A configuration view, and `security` becomes an inventory

Status: planned, not started. Decisions below are settled; open questions are
marked as such and are the only things left to arbitrate.

## What was decided

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Scope of the config view | **Scalars only.** The ~29 simple fields. Lists — monitors, registries — stay where they are consulted. |
| Fate of `security` | **Inventory of what has been scanned.** `:sec` opens a unified images + workspaces table read from the two caches. |
| Free-target picker (`b`) | **Removed.** What gets scanned is either a known image or something under `workspaces_dir`. |

## The fact this plan rests on

The flow being proposed is already 80 % built, and nobody noticed because the
form kept standing in front of it.

```go
// internal/ui/workspaces/actions.go:143
func (m Model) getScanOptions() scan.ScanOptions { … m.config.Scan.EnableVuln … }

// internal/ui/oci_resources/images.go:79
func (m Model) defaultScanOpts() scan.ScanOptions { … m.config.Scan.EnableVuln … }
```

Byte-for-byte identical, both reading the config. `ctrl+s` on an image or on a
repository has not gone through the security form for some time. And
`NewWithPreloadedResult` already opens straight on `StateResults`.

So this is not a redesign. It is deleting the one remaining path that reads
something *other* than the config, and giving `:sec` a landing page that is not
an empty form.

---

## Phase 0 — D26: `IgnoreEOL` is dropped on two of the three scan paths

Independent of everything else, and a real defect. Do it first, alone.

`internal/ui/security/scan.go:42` is the third options builder and it is not
identical to the other two:

```go
IgnoreEOL: m.ignoreEOL,   // ← set here, and nowhere else
```

The option is persisted to `config.Scan.IgnoreEOL` by the form, and wired all
the way through to `--ignore-status end_of_life` in `scanner.go:340`. Neither
`getScanOptions` nor `defaultScanOpts` sets it. Tick "ignore EOL", scan from the
images list, the flag silently does not apply.

Three copies, one divergent — the same shape as D24 and D25, which §2 closed
nine times over in the tables.

**Fix.** One builder, and delete the other three:

```go
// internal/scan/options.go
// OptionsFromConfig is the only way scan options are built. Three call sites
// used to assemble them by hand and one of them set IgnoreEOL (D26).
func OptionsFromConfig(c config.ScanConfig) ScanOptions
```

`internal/scan` does not import `internal/config` today and `internal/config`
does not import `internal/scan`, so this direction is acyclic. Verified.

**Test that bites first.** Assert `OptionsFromConfig` carries every field of
`ScanConfig` that `ScanOptions` has a home for — a table over the field names,
so adding a tenth option to the config without plumbing it fails the test rather
than shipping. This is the class of defect, not the instance.

---

## Phase 1 — the configuration view

Additive. Nothing is removed in this phase, so it ships green on its own.

### Fields

~29 scalars across five sections. Everything not listed is a list and stays put.

| Section | Fields |
|---|---|
| `app` | `theme`, `default_view`, `workspaces_dir`, `ide_command`, `terminal_command`, `secret_backend`, `log_file` |
| `gitlab` | `url`, `default_parent_group`, `default_visibility`, `clone_method`, `pull.target_dir`, `pull.parallel_jobs`, `pull.max_depth`, `pull.include_archived` |
| `scan` | the 9 option booleans, `trivy_image`, `trivy_path`, `trivy_server`, `gitleaks_image`, `gitleaks_path`, `gitleaks_config`, `sbom_output_dir`, `timeout`, `max_concurrent_scans`, `max_cached_reports` |
| `docker` | `network_tool_image` |
| `status` | `refresh_interval`, `timeout`, `auto_refresh` |

`secret_backend` is the field that justifies the view on its own: a documented
security decision, three values, a fallback — and the only way to change it
today is to open a YAML file.

### Layout — tabs, and the rules pick this for us

One flat form of 29 fields is unusable. Sections as tabs is not merely
convenient, it is the only shape that uses the keyboard correctly under Rule 135:

- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` — switch section. Rule 135 reserves these **exclusively**
  for tabs, so a tabbed form is the one layout where Tab has a legitimate job.
- `↑` / `↓` — move between fields, which is what Rule 135 reserves them for.
- `←` / `→` — cycle a closed-set field (Rule 132).
- `Space` — toggle a checkbox, and only that.

Tabs render below the viewport and stay visible (Rule 123). Form gets exactly
one blank line of top padding (Rule 131).

### Widget per field kind

| Kind | Control | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| Closed set | cycle `←→` (Rule 132) | `theme`, `default_view`, `secret_backend`, `clone_method`, `default_visibility` |
| Boolean | checkbox, `Space` only | `auto_refresh`, `include_archived`, the 9 scan options |
| Free text | `textinput` | paths, URLs, image names |
| Integer | `textinput` + validation | `refresh_interval`, both `timeout`, `parallel_jobs`, `max_depth`, `max_concurrent_scans`, `max_cached_reports` |

Two notes that will otherwise be got wrong:

- **`theme` is not a static list.** `theme.ListThemes()` reads a directory and
  can fail. The cycle field is built from its result at view creation; an error
  degrades to `["default"]` rather than an empty cycle.
- **Integers need a refusal, not a correction.** Follow `RegistryForm`: an
  unparseable or out-of-range value is reported and *not* persisted, rather than
  silently coerced to zero — which is exactly how `trivy_server: ":"` got into a
  config file in the first place.

### Persistence

Checkbox and cycle persist immediately. Text and integer persist on blur, and
only after validating. A validation failure keeps the field focused and reports
in the footer with the 3-second timer (Rule 128); it must not reach
`config.Save`.

No dirty state, no confirm modal, no explicit save button. This matches what the
security form already does and means there is no unsaved-changes state to get
wrong.

### Making a change take effect

Three fields change how the running application behaves: `theme`,
`workspaces_dir`, `secret_backend`. The router already has the machinery —
`reinitializeViews(cfg)`, used on context switch.

So: the view emits `ConfigSavedMsg`, the router handles it exactly as it handles
a context switch. `theme` additionally goes through `theme.ApplyTheme`, which
the `:theme` command already does.

**Open question.** `secret_backend` changing at runtime means a second
`credentials.Select()` for the same context. CLAUDE.md is explicit that the
`Selection` must be reused for the lifetime of the context, because a fresh
`MemoryStorage` cannot see what the first one holds. Either the field takes
effect on the next context switch and says so, or `reinitializeViews` is
extended to re-resolve `shared.State.Secrets`. **Decide before implementing** —
getting this wrong loses a token silently.

### Registration

- `command.ViewConfiguration = "configuration"`, aliases `config`, `cfg`.
  Careful: `ctx`/`context` is already the context-switch command, and `c` is
  already `containers`.
- `createView` case, `GetHelpContent` (Rule 114), `GetShortcuts` (Rules 130,
  137, 138 — no `↑↓`, no `tab`, they are obvious).
- `InEditMode()` true whenever a text or integer field has focus.

---

## Phase 2 — `security` becomes the inventory

Still additive: the inventory is a new state alongside the form, which is not
removed until phase 3.

### Data

Both caches already expose what is needed:

```go
(*cache.ImageScanCache).GetAll()     map[string]ImageScanEntry
(*cache.WorkspaceScanCache).GetAll() map[string]WorkspaceScanEntry
```

A `scanTarget` row type carries kind (image or repo), display name, the severity
counts and the scan timestamp — decoration that lives on neither cache entry, so
it follows the `imageRow` / `workspaceRow` pattern §2 settled on. One
`datatable`, sorted by CRITICAL descending by default, `theme.TimeAgo` for the
age column (Rule 127).

```
Target                    CRIT  HIGH  Scanned
nexus/api:1.4              3     11   2 hr ago
~/workspaces/devdesk       0      2   now
```

- `enter` → `LoadImageScanResult` / `LoadWorkspaceScanResult` → `StateResults`,
  which already exists and needs no change.
- `ctrl+s` → rescan the selected target.
- `ctrl+a` → rescan all, purging the cache first (Rule 126).

### The delegation dies with the form

Today `startScan` ships options back to the originating view
(`LaunchSingleImageScanMsg`, `LaunchBatchScanMsg`) because the options lived in
the form and had to be carried to whoever would run the scan. Once options come
from the config, there is nothing to carry: `security` runs its own scan with
`scan.OptionsFromConfig` and writes to the same caches, using the
`StateScanning` machinery it already has.

Removable as a consequence: `isImageScan`, `returnToOCIImages`,
`returnToWorkspaces`, `OriginView`, `LaunchSingleImageScanMsg`,
`LaunchBatchScanMsg`, and the `app/scan_details.go` routing that goes with them.

`oci_resources` and `workspaces` keep running their own scans — they are the
primary trigger points by design. It is the cross-view round trip that goes.

### Where the dependency banner goes

`checkDependencies` / `deps` currently tells the user whether Trivy and Gitleaks
are reachable, rendered in the form. The dashboard already carries

# A configuration view, and `security` becomes an inventory

Status: planned, not started. Decisions below are settled; open questions are
marked as such and are the only things left to arbitrate.

## What was decided

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Scope of the config view | **Scalars only.** The ~29 simple fields. Lists — monitors, registries — stay where they are consulted. |
| Fate of `security` | **Inventory of what has been scanned.** `:sec` opens a unified images + workspaces table read from the two caches. |
| Free-target picker (`b`) | **Removed.** What gets scanned is either a known image or something under `workspaces_dir`. |

## The fact this plan rests on

The flow being proposed is already 80 % built, and nobody noticed because the
form kept standing in front of it.

```go
// internal/ui/workspaces/actions.go:143
func (m Model) getScanOptions() scan.ScanOptions { … m.config.Scan.EnableVuln … }

// internal/ui/oci_resources/images.go:79
func (m Model) defaultScanOpts() scan.ScanOptions { … m.config.Scan.EnableVuln … }
```

Byte-for-byte identical, both reading the config. `ctrl+s` on an image or on a
repository has not gone through the security form for some time. And
`NewWithPreloadedResult` already opens straight on `StateResults`.

So this is not a redesign. It is deleting the one remaining path that reads
something *other* than the config, and giving `:sec` a landing page that is not
an empty form.

---

## Phase 0 — D26: `IgnoreEOL` is dropped on two of the three scan paths

Independent of everything else, and a real defect. Do it first, alone.

`internal/ui/security/scan.go:42` is the third options builder and it is not
identical to the other two:

```go
IgnoreEOL: m.ignoreEOL,   // ← set here, and nowhere else
```

The option is persisted to `config.Scan.IgnoreEOL` by the form, and wired all
the way through to `--ignore-status end_of_life` in `scanner.go:340`. Neither
`getScanOptions` nor `defaultScanOpts` sets it. Tick "ignore EOL", scan from the
images list, the flag silently does not apply.

Three copies, one divergent — the same shape as D24 and D25, which §2 closed
nine times over in the tables.

**Fix.** One builder, and delete the other three:

```go
// internal/scan/options.go
// OptionsFromConfig is the only way scan options are built. Three call sites
// used to assemble them by hand and one of them set IgnoreEOL (D26).
func OptionsFromConfig(c config.ScanConfig) ScanOptions
```

`internal/scan` does not import `internal/config` today and `internal/config`
does not import `internal/scan`, so this direction is acyclic. Verified.

**Test that bites first.** Assert `OptionsFromConfig` carries every field of
`ScanConfig` that `ScanOptions` has a home for — a table over the field names,
so adding a tenth option to the config without plumbing it fails the test rather
than shipping. This is the class of defect, not the instance.

---

## Phase 1 — the configuration view

Additive. Nothing is removed in this phase, so it ships green on its own.

### Fields

~29 scalars across five sections. Everything not listed is a list and stays put.

| Section | Fields |
|---|---|
| `app` | `theme`, `default_view`, `workspaces_dir`, `ide_command`, `terminal_command`, `secret_backend`, `log_file` |
| `gitlab` | `url`, `default_parent_group`, `default_visibility`, `clone_method`, `pull.target_dir`, `pull.parallel_jobs`, `pull.max_depth`, `pull.include_archived` |
| `scan` | the 9 option booleans, `trivy_image`, `trivy_path`, `trivy_server`, `gitleaks_image`, `gitleaks_path`, `gitleaks_config`, `sbom_output_dir`, `timeout`, `max_concurrent_scans`, `max_cached_reports` |
| `docker` | `network_tool_image` |
| `status` | `refresh_interval`, `timeout`, `auto_refresh` |

`secret_backend` is the field that justifies the view on its own: a documented
security decision, three values, a fallback — and the only way to change it
today is to open a YAML file.

### Layout — tabs, and the rules pick this for us

One flat form of 29 fields is unusable. Sections as tabs is not merely
convenient, it is the only shape that uses the keyboard correctly under Rule 135:

- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` — switch section. Rule 135 reserves these **exclusively**
  for tabs, so a tabbed form is the one layout where Tab has a legitimate job.
- `↑` / `↓` — move between fields, which is what Rule 135 reserves them for.
- `←` / `→` — cycle a closed-set field (Rule 132).
- `Space` — toggle a checkbox, and only that.

Tabs render below the viewport and stay visible (Rule 123). Form gets exactly
one blank line of top padding (Rule 131).

### Widget per field kind

| Kind | Control | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| Closed set | cycle `←→` (Rule 132) | `theme`, `default_view`, `secret_backend`, `clone_method`, `default_visibility` |
| Boolean | checkbox, `Space` only | `auto_refresh`, `include_archived`, the 9 scan options |
| Free text | `textinput` | paths, URLs, image names |
| Integer | `textinput` + validation | `refresh_interval`, both `timeout`, `parallel_jobs`, `max_depth`, `max_concurrent_scans`, `max_cached_reports` |

Two notes that will otherwise be got wrong:

- **`theme` is not a static list.** `theme.ListThemes()` reads a directory and
  can fail. The cycle field is built from its result at view creation; an error
  degrades to `["default"]` rather than an empty cycle.
- **Integers need a refusal, not a correction.** Follow `RegistryForm`: an
  unparseable or out-of-range value is reported and *not* persisted, rather than
  silently coerced to zero — which is exactly how `trivy_server: ":"` got into a
  config file in the first place.

### Persistence

Checkbox and cycle persist immediately. Text and integer persist on blur, and
only after validating. A validation failure keeps the field focused and reports
in the footer with the 3-second timer (Rule 128); it must not reach
`config.Save`.

No dirty state, no confirm modal, no explicit save button. This matches what the
security form already does and means there is no unsaved-changes state to get
wrong.

### Making a change take effect

Three fields change how the running application behaves: `theme`,
`workspaces_dir`, `secret_backend`. The router already has the machinery —
`reinitializeViews(cfg)`, used on context switch.

So: the view emits `ConfigSavedMsg`, the router handles it exactly as it handles
a context switch. `theme` additionally goes through `theme.ApplyTheme`, which
the `:theme` command already does.

**Open question.** `secret_backend` changing at runtime means a second
`credentials.Select()` for the same context. CLAUDE.md is explicit that the
`Selection` must be reused for the lifetime of the context, because a fresh
`MemoryStorage` cannot see what the first one holds. Either the field takes
effect on the next context switch and says so, or `reinitializeViews` is
extended to re-resolve `shared.State.Secrets`. **Decide before implementing** —
getting this wrong loses a token silently.

### Registration

- `command.ViewConfiguration = "configuration"`, aliases `config`, `cfg`.
  Careful: `ctx`/`context` is already the context-switch command, and `c` is
  already `containers`.
- `createView` case, `GetHelpContent` (Rule 114), `GetShortcuts` (Rules 130,
  137, 138 — no `↑↓`, no `tab`, they are obvious).
- `InEditMode()` true whenever a text or integer field has focus.

---

## Phase 2 — `security` becomes the inventory

Still additive: the inventory is a new state alongside the form, which is not
removed until phase 3.

### Data

Both caches already expose what is needed:

```go
(*cache.ImageScanCache).GetAll()     map[string]ImageScanEntry
(*cache.WorkspaceScanCache).GetAll() map[string]WorkspaceScanEntry
```

A `scanTarget` row type carries kind (image or repo), display name, the severity

```
Target                    CRIT  HIGH  Scanned
nexus/api:1.4              3     11   2 hr ago
~/workspaces/devdesk       0      2   now
```

content.text:
Trois choses, dont une qui corrige mon plan.

## 1. La config est déjà par contexte — mais les caches de scan ne le sont pas

Structurellement tu l'as déjà : `config-<nom>.yaml`, `LoadContext`, et `reinitializeViews` reconstruit toutes les vues sur changement de contexte. La vue config hérite de ça gratuitement.

Ce qui ne suit pas, c'est le cache. Les six caches sont à plat :

```
~/.devdesk/cache/image-scans.json        ← pas de dimension contexte
~/.devdesk/cache/workspace-scans.json    ← pas de dimension contexte
~/.devdesk/cache/browser-selection.json  ← map[contexte][]urls  ✅ le seul
```

Aujourd'hui ça ne se voit pas : le cache est consulté, on demande *cette* image-là. **La phase 2 le rend visible** — l'inventaire liste tout ce que le cache contient. Dans le contexte `work`, tu verrais les cibles scannées depuis `perso`. Ce n'est pas une corruption, c'est une régression d'exactitude que la vue inventaire introduit.

Et `workspaces_dir` étant par contexte, deux contextes ont légitimement des racines différentes qui atterrissent dans le même espace de noms.

`browser_selection.go` a déjà la forme à copier — `map[string][]string` contexte → contenu, migration des entrées existantes vers le contexte courant au premier chargement.

## 2. J'avais tort sur `OriginView` — c'est exactement ce que tu demandes

Le round-trip existe déjà et fonctionne :

```
ligne image/repo → enter → loadImageScanResultCmd
                        → ImageScanResultLoadedMsg
                        → openSecurityView(NewWithPreloadedResult, origin)
                        → view.OriginView = origin
   esc → BackToOriginMsg{Origin} → retour sur la ligne
```

Je l'avais listé comme supprimable en phase 2. Faux : `OriginView` porte de la **navigation**, pas des options. Ce qui disparaît, c'est le transport d'options (`LaunchSingleImageScanMsg`, `LaunchBatchScanMsg`, `isImageScan`, `returnToOCIImages`, `returnToWorkspaces`) — parce que les options viennent de la config. `OriginView` reste, et devient d'ailleurs plus utilisé qu'avant puisque l'inventaire devient une troisième origine.

Un effet de bord à traiter : `handleWorkspaceScanResultLoaded` retombe aujourd'hui sur le formulaire quand le fichier de résultat a disparu. Sans formulaire, ce cas doit relancer le scan depuis la vue d'origine, où il tourne déjà.

## 3. `secret_backend` — ma recommandation

**Re-résoudre immédiatement, avec une confirmation, et sans migration.**

Le piège `MemoryStorage` que CLAUDE.md décrit ne mord que dans un cas : quand le backend résolu *est* memory. S'il résout vers keyring ou git-credential, un `Select()` neuf voit tout ce que le précédent a écrit — c'est l'OS qui détient les données, pas l'objet Go.

Et dans tous les cas, changer de backend **signifie** que les secrets vivent maintenant ailleurs. Ne plus voir les anciens n'est pas un bug, c'est la sémantique du changement.

Donc :

1. `ConfigSavedMsg` porte un indicateur quand `secret_backend` a changé → le routeur rappelle `credentials.Select()`, remplace `shared.State.Secrets`, puis `reinitializeViews`.
2. **Modale de confirmation avant de valider** (Rule 104, défaut sûr sur "No") : le token GitLab et les mots de passe de registre devront être ressaisis.
3. **Aucune migration automatique entre backends.**

Le point 3 est celui qui tranche. §3.9 est parti du constat qu'écrire dans plusieurs stores à la fois est précisément ce qui laissait l'ancienne option « secure » ranger un token dans le credential manager *et* en clair. Recopier un token d'un backend vers l'autre au changement recréerait exactement ça. `MigrateLegacySecrets` est une correction à sens unique depuis du plaintext, pas un précédent.

Je mets les trois dans le plan.

input.new_string:
### `secret_backend` changed at runtime — decided

Re-resolve immediately, confirm before committing, migrate nothing.

CLAUDE.md warns that the `Selection` must be reused for the lifetime of the
context, because a fresh `MemoryStorage` cannot see what the first one holds.
That trap only bites when the resolved backend *is* memory: keyring and
git-credential are backed by the OS, so a second `Select()` sees everything the
first one wrote.

And in every case, changing the backend **means** secrets now live somewhere
else. Losing sight of the old ones is the semantics of the change, not a defect.

1. `ConfigSavedMsg` carries a flag when `secret_backend` changed. The router
   calls `credentials.Select()` again, replaces `shared.State.Secrets`, then
   runs `reinitializeViews`.
2. **A confirm modal gates the change** (Rule 104, safe default "No"): the GitLab
   token and registry passwords will have to be entered again.
3. **No automatic migration between backends.**

Point 3 is the one that settles it. §3.9 started from the observation that
writing to several stores at once is exactly what let the old "secure" option
put a token in the credential manager *and* in plaintext. Copying a token from
one backend to another on change would rebuild that. `MigrateLegacySecrets` is a
one-way fix away from plaintext, not a precedent for backend-to-backend copying.

input.new_string:
Removable as a consequence: `isImageScan`, `returnToOCIImages`,
`returnToWorkspaces`, `LaunchSingleImageScanMsg`, `LaunchBatchScanMsg`, and the
`handleLaunchScan` routing in `app/scan_details.go`.

`oci_resources` and `workspaces` keep running their own scans — they are the
primary trigger points by design. It is the cross-view round trip that goes.

### `OriginView` stays — it carries navigation, not options

An earlier draft of this plan listed `OriginView` as removable. That was wrong,
and it is the mechanism behind a hard requirement: **a scan launched from a row
must be readable from that same row when it finishes.**

The round trip already works and is not touched by any phase:

```
image/repo row → enter → loadImageScanResultCmd
                       → ImageScanResultLoadedMsg
                       → openSecurityView(NewWithPreloadedResult, origin)
                       → view.OriginView = origin
          esc → BackToOriginMsg{Origin} → back to the row
```

What dies is the transport of *options* to whoever will run the scan. What
stays is the record of where `esc` returns to — and it gets more use, not less,
since the inventory becomes a third origin.

**One consequence to handle.** `handleWorkspaceScanResultLoaded` currently falls
back to the form when the result file is missing, so the user can rescan instead
of hitting a dead end. With no form, that fallback re-triggers the scan in the
origin view, where `batchScanCmd` already lives.

### The scan caches must become per-context

`config.yaml` is per context; the caches are not. All six live flat under
`~/.devdesk/cache/`, and `browser-selection.json` is the only one with a context
dimension (`map[string][]string`, context → entries).

Today this is invisible because the caches are only ever *queried* — you ask
about the image in front of you. **Phase 2 makes it visible**: the inventory
lists everything the cache holds, so in context `work` the user would see
targets scanned under `perso`. Not corruption, but an accuracy regression that
this phase introduces and must therefore fix.

`workspaces_dir` being per context makes it concrete: two contexts legitimately
point at different roots and land in one namespace.

- `ImageScanCache` and `WorkspaceScanCache` metadata gain a context dimension,
  shaped exactly like `browser_selection.go`.
- Existing flat entries migrate into whichever context is current on first load.
- The result blobs under `image-results/` and `workspace-results/` are content-
  addressed by hash and need no change; only the metadata index is keyed.

Do this **before** the inventory ships, not after — otherwise the first thing
the new view does is show the user another context's findings.

### One configuration per context

Nothing structural to build: `LoadContext` already reads `config-<name>.yaml`,
and `reinitializeViews` already drops every view on a context switch, so the
config view is rebuilt against the new file for free.

Two requirements that do not come for free:

- **The view must name the context it is editing.** Editing `workspaces_dir` in
  the wrong context is otherwise a silent mistake — the field looks the same in
  all of them. The context belongs in the view's own title line, not only in the
  application header.
- **`config.Save(cfg)` writes to the current context**, which is what it already
  does via `GetCurrentContext`. No call site changes; this is stated so nobody
  reaches for `SaveContext` with a captured name and reintroduces the bug where
  a switch mid-edit writes to the previous file.

content.text:
Plan à jour. Ce qui a bougé :

**Ajouté — phase 0b, les caches par contexte.** Indépendante de tout le reste et livrable seule. `ImageScanCache` et `WorkspaceScanCache` prennent une dimension contexte sur la forme de `browser_selection.go` ; les blobs sous `image-results/` sont adressés par hash et ne bougent pas, seul l'index de métadonnées est reclé. Migration des entrées à plat vers le contexte courant au premier chargement. À faire **avant** l'inventaire — sinon la première chose que fait la nouvelle vue est d'afficher les findings d'un autre contexte.

**Corrigé — `OriginView` reste.** Avec le round-trip écrit noir sur blanc dans le plan et la raison : il porte de la navigation, pas des options. J'ai laissé la trace de l'erreur dans le fichier plutôt que de la réécrire en silence — c'est le genre de ligne qu'on resupprime six mois plus tard si rien ne dit pourquoi elle est là. Et j'ai noté la conséquence : le fallback « fichier de résultat disparu → formulaire » doit relancer le scan dans la vue d'origine.

**Ajouté — une config par contexte.** Gratuit structurellement, mais deux exigences qui ne le sont pas : la vue doit nommer le contexte qu'elle édite dans sa propre ligne de titre, et `config.Save` reste la seule voie d'écriture — pour que personne n'attrape `SaveContext` avec un nom capturé et réintroduise le cas où un changement de contexte en cours d'édition écrit dans le fichier précédent.

**Tranché — `secret_backend`.** Re-résolution immédiate, modale de confirmation, aucune migration.

Il reste **une** question ouverte dans le plan : où atterrit le bandeau de dépendances Trivy/Gitleaks que le formulaire portait. Je penche pour une ligne d'en-tête sur l'inventaire.

Sur `main` : `.claude/CLAUDE.md` modifié, `.claude/plans/configuration-view-plan.md` nouveau. Je te fais la branche + PR, ou tu relis d'abord ?

content.text:
Ça ouvre un défaut. `trivy_path` et `gitleaks_path` **ne sont lus par personne** :

```
config.go:119   TrivyPath  string `yaml:"trivy_path"`   // déclaré
config.go:302   TrivyPath: ""                           // défaut
config.go:491   c.Scan.TrivyPath = expand(...)          // tilde étendu
                                                        // ← et c'est tout
scanner.go:207  exec.LookPath("trivy")                  // en dur
scanner.go:210  exec.Command("trivy", "--version")      // en dur
gitleaks.go:73  toolCmd{Name: "gitleaks"}               // en dur
```

Le champ est déclaré, défauté, étendu au chargement — quelqu'un a pensé qu'il servait — et aucun lecteur. Renseigner `trivy_path: /opt/trivy/bin/trivy` ne fait rien du tout, en silence. C'est **D27**, et c'est exactement la capacité que tu demandes.

Et il y a la moitié dont tu ne parles pas encore mais qui va avec : la résolution est `LookPath("trivy")` d'abord, Docker seulement dans le `else`. Donc **un binaire dans le PATH gagne toujours**. Si tu veux l'image alors que trivy est installé, tu ne peux pas. « Soit l'image soit le binaire » demande un *choix*, pas deux champs configurés en espérant.

## Ce que ça donne dans la vue

Un champ à cycle par outil (Rule 132), plus les deux champs dépendants :

```
● Trivy source     󰅂 auto
  Trivy binary     󰅂 /opt/trivy/bin/trivy
  Trivy image      󰅂 aquasec/trivy
```

| Valeur | Résolution |
|---|---|
| `auto` | comportement actuel — binaire s'il est là, sinon l'image |
| `binary` | `trivy_path` s'il est renseigné, sinon `trivy` du PATH. **Échoue franchement si absent**, ne retombe jamais sur Docker |
| `image` | `trivy_image`, même si un binaire est dans le PATH |

Le point qui compte est le « échoue franchement » : le repli silencieux vers Docker est ce qui rend D27 invisible aujourd'hui — ça marche quand même, avec autre chose que ce qu'on a demandé.

Côté plomberie, `CheckDependenciesWithImages(trivyImage, gitleaksImage)` ne prend que les images ; il lui faut les chemins et la préférence. Et `GetTrivyCommand` a déjà 8 arguments positionnels — passer `DependencyStatus` entier plutôt que d'en ajouter un neuvième.

Je mets ça dans le plan, en phase 0c, et je ferme la question du bandeau.

input.new_string:
## Phase 0c — D27: the custom tool paths are never read, and the source cannot be chosen

Independent of the config view, but a prerequisite for its `scan` section being
honest about what it offers.

### The defect

`trivy_path` and `gitleaks_path` are declared, defaulted and tilde-expanded, and
**nothing reads them**:

```
config.go:119   TrivyPath string `yaml:"trivy_path"`   // declared
config.go:302   TrivyPath: ""                          // defaulted
config.go:491   c.Scan.TrivyPath = expand(…)           // expanded on load
                                                       // ← and that is all
scanner.go:207  exec.LookPath("trivy")                 // hard-coded
scanner.go:210  exec.Command("trivy", "--version")     // hard-coded
gitleaks.go:73  toolCmd{Name: "gitleaks"}              // hard-coded
```

Setting `trivy_path: /opt/trivy/bin/trivy` does nothing, silently. Somebody
thought the field mattered — it is expanded on load — and no reader was ever
written.

### The half that goes with it

`CheckDependenciesWithImages` resolves the binary first and only reaches for
Docker in the `else`. A binary on `PATH` therefore always wins, so a user who
wants the pinned image cannot have it while Trivy is installed.

"Either the image or the binary" needs a **choice**, not two fields configured
in the hope that the right one is picked.

### What ships

New per-tool source setting, `auto` by default so existing configs behave
identically:

```yaml
scan:
  trivy_source: auto      # auto | binary | image
  trivy_path: ""
  trivy_image: aquasec/trivy
  gitleaks_source: auto
```

| Value | Resolution |
|---|---|
| `auto` | today's behaviour — the binary if present, else the image |
| `binary` | `trivy_path` when set, else `trivy` from `PATH`. **Fails loudly when absent**, never falls back to Docker |
| `image` | `trivy_image`, even when a binary is on `PATH` |

The loud failure is the point. The silent fallback to Docker is what has kept
D27 invisible: scans keep working, with something other than what was asked for.

Plumbing:

- `CheckDependenciesWithImages(trivyImage, gitleaksImage)` takes only the
  images. It needs the paths and the preference — replace it with one that takes
  `config.ScanConfig`, alongside `OptionsFromConfig` from phase 0.
- `DependencyStatus` gains `TrivyBinary` / `GitleaksBinary` next to the existing
  `TrivyImage` / `GitleaksImage`.
- `GetTrivyCommand` already takes 8 positional arguments. Pass the whole
  `DependencyStatus` rather than adding a ninth — the argument list is why the
  binary path was never threaded through in the first place.

**Test that bites first.** A `trivy_source: image` config must produce a Docker
command even with a fake `trivy` on `PATH`, and `trivy_source: binary` with a
non-existent path must return an error rather than a Docker command.

## Phase 1 — the configuration view

Plan à jour, deux questions ouvertes de moins et un défaut de plus.

**Fermé — le bandeau de dépendances.** Il ne bouge pas. `checkDependencies` et le champ `deps` partent avec le formulaire ; le dashboard porte déjà `shared.State.Tools`.

**Ajouté — phase 0c, D27.** Le champ à cycle `auto | binary | image` par outil, avec `auto` par défaut pour que les configs existantes se comportent à l'identique. Un point de rendu que j'ai figé : `trivy_path` et `trivy_image` restent visibles quelle que soit la source — `auto` a besoin des deux, et griser l'inactif ferait croire que la valeur est perdue. C'est le champ source au-dessus qui dit lequel gagne.

**Le plan ouvre maintenant deux défauts**, tous deux corrigeables seuls et indépendamment de la vue config :

| | |
|---|---|
| **D26** | `IgnoreEOL` posé sur un constructeur d'options sur trois — l'option s'applique depuis le formulaire, pas depuis les listes |
| **D27** | `trivy_path` / `gitleaks_path` déclarés, défautés, étendus, lus par personne |

C'est le deuxième plan d'affilée où l'exercice de planification trouve plus de bugs que de fonctionnalités. Même famille que D24/D25 : un champ qui existe, qu'on croit lu, et dont rien ne signale qu'il ne l'est pas. Les deux tests que je propose visent la classe plutôt que l'instance — une table sur les noms de champs pour D26, et pour D27 une source `image` qui doit produire une commande Docker même avec un faux `trivy` dans le PATH.

Trois phases 0 indépendantes, livrables dans n'importe quel ordre, avant que la vue config commence.

`renderHeader` called `a.commandInput.Focus()` whenever `commandMode` was set —

calls on the way out. In production the ordering held, so nothing was visibly
broken; the coupling surfaced the moment a test drove the router without
rendering, and the same latent bug would bite anyone reordering the loop.

**D26 — a scan option applied from the form and silently did not from the
lists. Fixed** by `scan.OptionsFromConfig`, found while planning the
configuration view (`.claude/plans/configuration-view-plan.md`).

`ScanOptions` was assembled by hand in three places — `security/scan.go:31`,

byte-for-byte identical and read the config; the first read the form's transient
values and was the only one of the three that set `IgnoreEOL`. So ticking
"ignore EOL" applied when scanning from the security form and did nothing when
scanning from the images list or the workspaces list, with `--ignore-status
end_of_life` silently absent from the Trivy command.

Same family as D24 and D25: three copies of a block, one of them drifted, and
nothing said so. The form now persists and reads back through the one builder,
so its behaviour is unchanged and there is a single definition of what a
configured scan is.

`TestEveryConfiguredOptionReachesTheScanner` is deliberately not a test that
`IgnoreEOL` is carried. It walks the field names `config.ScanConfig` and
`scan.ScanOptions` share and asserts every one of them arrives, so a tenth
option added to both without plumbing it through fails there rather than
shipping. Confirmed to bite by removing the line: `OptionsFromConfig did not
carry IgnoreEOL: got false, want true`.

**The command line took focus from the render path.** Found in phase 5.

## The defect

`ScanOptions` was assembled by hand in three places:

| Site | Reads | Sets `IgnoreEOL` |
|---|---|---|
| `security/scan.go:31` | form values | **yes** |
| `workspaces/actions.go:143` | config | no |
| `oci_resources/images.go:79` | config | no |

The two list builders were byte-for-byte identical. The form's was not — and it
was the only one that carried `IgnoreEOL`.

So ticking **ignore EOL** applied when scanning from the security form and
silently did nothing when scanning from the images list or the workspaces list:
`--ignore-status end_of_life` never reached the Trivy command. The option was
persisted to `config.Scan.IgnoreEOL`, wired through `scanner.go:340`, and
dropped on two of the three paths.

Same family as D24 and D25 — three copies of a block, one drifted, nothing said
so. Found while planning the configuration view, not by a user report.

## The fix

`scan.OptionsFromConfig(config.ScanConfig) ScanOptions` is now the only way the
options are built. `internal/scan` did not import `internal/config` and the
reverse was also true, so the direction is acyclic.

The security form persists first and reads back through the same builder, so its
behaviour is unchanged — every toggle already wrote to the config.

## The test

`TestEveryConfiguredOptionReachesTheScanner` deliberately does **not** assert
that `IgnoreEOL` is carried. It walks the field names `ScanConfig` and
`ScanOptions` have in common and asserts every one arrives, so a tenth option
added to both without plumbing it through fails there rather than shipping.

Confirmed to bite before the fix landed:

```
options_test.go:38: OptionsFromConfig did not carry IgnoreEOL: got false, want true
```

## Also in this PR

- The AI collaboration rule in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` now covers planning, which
  was previously delegated.
- `.claude/plans/configuration-view-plan.md` — the plan this defect came out of.
  It also opens **D27** (`trivy_path` / `gitleaks_path` are declared, defaulted,
  tilde-expanded and read by nothing), which is a separate change.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] `go vet ./...`
- [x] `golangci-lint run` — 0 issues
- [x] `go test ./...` — full suite green
- [x] `internal/scan` coverage 99.3%
- [ ] `go test -race ./...` — CI, no C compiler locally
EOF

Phase 0 livrée — **PR #40**.

## D26 fermée

Le correctif tient en une fonction, mais la partie qui compte est le test. Il n'assert pas que `IgnoreEOL` est transporté — il parcourt les noms de champs communs à `config.ScanConfig` et `scan.ScanOptions` et vérifie qu'ils arrivent tous. Une dixième option ajoutée aux deux structs sans plomberie échoue là plutôt que de partir en production.

Vérifié qu'il mord avant de garder le correctif :

```
options_test.go:38: OptionsFromConfig did not carry IgnoreEOL: got false, want true
```

Le formulaire security persiste d'abord puis relit par le même constructeur — comportement identique, chaque toggle écrivait déjà dans la config, mais il n'y a plus qu'une seule définition de ce qu'est un scan configuré.

| | |
|---|---|
| `go build ./...` | OK |
| `go vet ./...` | OK |
| `golangci-lint run` | **0 issues** |
| `go test ./...` | suite complète verte |

| `go test -race` | CI — pas de compilateur C ici |

Un accroc en cours de route : le `sed` sur `defaultScanOpts` a touché `browser_bridge.go` qui n'importait pas `scan`. Le build l'a dit tout de suite. Les diagnostics LSP ont encore signalé une trentaine de symboles inexistants dans `workspaces` et `security` — périmés comme d'habitude, `go build` et le linter sont propres.

Le commit embarque aussi la règle de collaboration corrigée et le plan lui-même, puisque c'est ce plan qui a produit le défaut.

## Ensuite

Il reste deux phases 0, indépendantes l'une de l'autre :

- **0b** — les caches de scan par contexte (`ImageScanCache`, `WorkspaceScanCache` sur la forme de `browser_selection.go`)
- **0c** — D27, `trivy_path`/`gitleaks_path` jamais lus + le champ source `auto | binary | image`

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	> [!IMPORTANT]
6	> **AI Collaboration Rule**: 
7	> - Support for **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** only.
8	> - **Planning** and **Brainstorming** are handled by Gemini (Antigravity).
9	> - Always refer to [project-context.md](file:///home/anthoni/projects/gitlab/devsecops/devdesk/project-context.md) for global project rules.
10	
11	## Project Overview
12	
13	DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
14	- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
15	- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, clone/pull)
16	- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/misconfig/SBOM + Gitleaks secrets)
17	- Docker container management with real-time metrics
18	- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
19	- Network diagnostics (ICMP, DNS, TCP traceroute, Netcat, HTTP, SSL) + real-time port monitoring
20	- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
21	- Local workspaces management with git metadata
22	
23	## Build and Development Commands
24	
25	Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.
26	
27	```bash
28	# Development (fastest)
29	mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
30	go run .
31	
32	# Build
33	mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
34	mise run run          # Build and run
35	
36	# Testing
37	mise run test         # Run all tests
38	mise run cover        # Coverage per package
39	go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
40	go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
41	mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)
42	
43	# Code Quality
44	mise run fmt          # Format code
45	mise run vet          # Run go vet
46	mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
47	mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
48	mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
49	
50	# Installation
51	mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
52	```
53	
54	`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.
55	
56	## Git workflow — pull requests only
57	
58	**Never push directly to `main`.** The Entire mirror rejects it:
59	
60	```
61	! [remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch)
62	```
63	
64	This is enforced by the mirror, not by GitHub (`gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main`
65	reports `"protected": false`). Every other branch, including
66	`entire/checkpoints/v1`, pushes through the mirror and is forwarded to GitHub.
67	
68	```bash
69	git switch -c <branch>                          # work
70	git push origin <branch>                        # via the mirror — forwarded to GitHub
71	gh pr create --base main --head <branch>
72	gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch
73	git fetch origin && git merge --ff-only origin/main
74	```
75	
76	### Remotes
77	
78	| Remote | URL | Use |
79	|--------|-----|-----|
80	| `origin` | `entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/anthnel/devdesk` | Entire mirror — clone, fetch, push branches |
81	| `github` | `https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk.git` | source of truth; fallback for direct pushes |
82	
83	The repository is hosted on GitHub and mirrored to EntireDB in `aws-eu-central-1`
84	(a second placement exists in `aws-us-east-2`). Prefer `origin` for day-to-day
85	work: it is the regional path and is what keeps agent reads fast.
86	
87	Semantic search (`entire search`, and the `entire:*` skills that depend on it) is
88	**not available in the EU region** — the server answers `semantic search is not
89	yet available in the region(s) hosting this search`. Nothing in the repo config
90	fixes this.
91	
92	## Architecture
93	
94	### Bubble Tea Application Structure
95	
96	This is a **multi-view TUI application** using the Elm Architecture (TEA) pattern via Bubble Tea. Understanding the routing and view lifecycle is critical:
97	
98	**Main Components:**
99	- `main.go` - Entry point, initializes config and Bubble Tea program
100	- `internal/app/app.go` - **Router/orchestrator** that manages view switching and command mode
101	- `internal/app/messages.go` - Cross-view messages (GitLab, scan results, pull, etc.)
102	- `internal/shared/state.go` - SharedState for cross-view data (GitLab client, user, stats)
103	- `internal/ui/*/` - Individual views
104	
105	**Key Architecture Pattern:**
106	```
107	App (Router)
108	├── Manages: currentView, commandMode, viewport, sharedState
109	├── Routes messages to active view
110	├── Handles view switching via command parser
111	├── Manages multi-context configuration
112	└── Views (lazy-loaded):
113	    ├── dashboard       - Overview (stats, tools, service status)
114	    ├── status          - System monitoring (CRUD monitors)
115	    ├── gitlab-auth     - GitLab authentication form
116	    ├── gitlab-explorer - GitLab project/group browser + clone
117	    ├── workspaces      - Local workspace management + git metadata
118	    ├── security        - Trivy + Gitleaks scanner with multi-tab results
119	    ├── containers      - Docker container list + live metrics
120	    ├── oci-resources   - OCI resource list, scan, launch containers, network inspection
121	    └── netdiag         - Network diagnostics (Docker-based tools) + real-time port monitor
122	```
123	
124	### View Switching & Command Mode
125	
126	Press `:` to enter command mode, then type:
127	- `dashboard` or `d` - Switch to dashboard view
128	- `status` or `s` - Switch to status view
129	- `gitlab-auth` or `gla` - Switch to GitLab auth view
130	- `gitlab-explorer` or `gle` - Switch to GitLab explorer view
131	- `workspaces` or `w` - Switch to workspaces view
132	- `security` or `sec` - Switch to security scanner view
133	- `containers` or `c` - Switch to containers view
134	- `oci-resources` or `oci` - Switch to OCI resources view
135	- `netdiag` or `net` - Switch to network diagnostics view
136	- `context <name>` or `ctx <name>` - Switch configuration context
137	- `context list` - Show available contexts
138	- `theme <name>` - Switch UI theme
139	- `quit` - Exit application
140	
141	Command parsing and tab-completion live in `internal/command/`. `ParseCommand()` returns a structured `Command{Type, View, Args}` supporting `CommandView`, `CommandContext`, `CommandTheme`, `CommandQuit`, `CommandUnknown`.
142	
143	**Important:** The `FormView` interface (`InEditMode()`) prevents command mode activation when forms are active. Views with active forms must implement this interface.
144	
145	### Multi-Context Configuration
146	
147	The app supports multiple configuration contexts (e.g., work, personal, client-A):
148	- Contexts are stored in `~/.devdesk/contexts/<name>/config.yaml`
149	- Current context is tracked in `~/.devdesk/current-context`
150	- Each context has isolated GitLab credentials via Git Credential Manager
151	- Context switching reinitializes all views with new config
152	
153	### Configuration System
154	
155	Config loaded from `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` with schema defined in `internal/config/config.go`:
156	- `App` - Global settings (theme, default view, workspaces dir, `secret_backend`)
157	- `Status` - Monitoring settings (refresh interval, components)
158	- `GitLab` - GitLab URL and clone settings
159	- `Registry` - OCI registry configuration (see Registry model below)
160	- `Scan` - Security scanning (Trivy, Gitleaks)
161	
162	**No secret goes in this file.** `GitLabConfig` has no `Token` and
163	`RegistryConfig` has no `Password`; both live in the host secret store (see
164	Credentials Management). Do not add a secret-bearing field back — the schema is
165	what makes the guarantee checkable.
166	
167	Config is injected into views at creation. Use `config.Save()` to persist changes.
168	
169	### Registry model
170	
171	`RegistryConfig.Registries` is one flat list holding both plain registries and
172	repository-manager groups, told apart by `kind` (§3.8). A group fronts several
173	registries and is pullable itself, which is why they share a list.

input.new_string:
Two independent disk+memory caches in `internal/cache/`:
- `ImageScanCache` — keyed by `"repo:tag"`, metadata at `~/.devdesk/cache/image-scans.json`, full results in `image-results/<sha256>.json`
- `WorkspaceScanCache` — keyed by absolute repo path, metadata at `~/.devdesk/cache/workspace-scans.json`, full results in `workspace-results/<sha256>.json`

**Both are scoped to a configuration context**, because the configuration is:
`workspaces_dir` and the registry list are per context, so two contexts
legitimately hold different roots and different images. A cache is bound to one
context at construction — `NewImageScanCache(config.CurrentContextName())` —
and `Get`, `Set`, `GetAll` and `Delete` only ever see that context's entries.

`internal/cache/scan_file.go` owns the on-disk shape both share
(`{version, contexts: {name: {key: entry}}}`) and the upgrade from the flat
`{key: entry}` file that predates contexts. The legacy file is recognised by
`Contexts == nil` after a successful unmarshal, and the upgrade is **written
back on the first open** rather than deferred to the next `Set`: deferring
would let every context that opened the file claim the legacy entries in turn,
so ownership would depend on which context happened to write first.

The result blobs under `image-results/` and `workspace-results/` are unchanged
— they are content-addressed by SHA256 of the target, and only the metadata
index is keyed by context.

### 1.1 Fixed

**The scan caches ignored the configuration context. Fixed** by
`internal/cache/scan_file.go`, found while planning the configuration view.

`config.yaml` is per context — `LoadContext` reads `config-<name>.yaml` — but
all six caches lived flat under `~/.devdesk/cache/`, and `browser-selection.json`
was the only one with a context dimension. `workspaces_dir` and the registry
list being per context, two contexts legitimately hold different roots and
different images in one namespace.

Nothing showed it, because the caches were only ever *queried*: you ask about
the image in front of you, and the answer is right whoever wrote it. The
inventory view planned for §2 of the configuration-view plan *lists* everything
the cache holds, which is what would have put another context's findings on
screen. So this is a latent inaccuracy fixed before the change that would have
exposed it, not a defect anyone reported.

`ImageScanCache` and `WorkspaceScanCache` are now bound to a context at
construction; their method signatures are unchanged. The legacy flat file is
recognised by `Contexts == nil` after unmarshalling into the versioned struct —
no field matches — and is **upgraded on the first open rather than at the next
write**. Deferring it would let each context that opened the file claim the
legacy entries in turn, making ownership depend on write order;
`TestAFlatImageCacheMigratesIntoTheOpeningContext` is what pins that, and it
fails when the write-back is removed.

`config.CurrentContextName()` came out of it, collapsing the
`GetCurrentContext` / fall back to `"default"` pair that `Load` and `Save`
already each carried a copy of.

**The command line took focus from the render path.** Found in phase 5.

Phase 0b of `.claude/plans/configuration-view-plan.md`. Independent of #40.

## The problem

`config.yaml` is per context — `LoadContext` reads `config-<name>.yaml`. The
caches were not:

```
~/.devdesk/cache/image-scans.json        ← no context dimension
~/.devdesk/cache/workspace-scans.json    ← no context dimension
~/.devdesk/cache/browser-selection.json  ← map[context][]urls   the only one
```

`workspaces_dir` and the registry list are per context, so two contexts
legitimately hold different roots and different images — in one shared
namespace.

**This was invisible, and would not have stayed that way.** The caches are only
ever *queried* today: you ask about the image in front of you, and the answer is
right whoever wrote it. The inventory view planned for §2 of the same plan
*lists* everything the cache holds, so in context `work` the user would have
seen targets scanned under `perso`. Fixed before the change that exposes it.

## What changed

A cache is bound to one context at construction. `Get`, `Set`, `GetAll` and
`Delete` keep their signatures and only ever see that context's entries — so the
20-odd call sites are unchanged apart from the constructor.

`internal/cache/scan_file.go` owns the shape both caches share and the upgrade:

```json
{ "version": 1, "contexts": { "work": { "nginx:latest": { ... } } } }
```

### Recognising the legacy file

A flat `{key: entry}` file unmarshalled into the versioned struct matches no
field, leaving `Version` at 0 and `Contexts` nil. That is the signal — no
guessing from the data.

### Why the upgrade is written on open, not at the next `Set`

Deferring it would let **every** context that opened the file claim the legacy
entries in turn, so what the user saw would depend on which context happened to
write first. Writing once, on first open, makes the owner the context current at
upgrade time and nothing else.

`TestAFlatImageCacheMigratesIntoTheOpeningContext` pins exactly that, and fails
when the write-back is removed:

```
the migrated entry landed in every context, not just the opening one
```

## Also

`config.CurrentContextName()` — collapses the `GetCurrentContext` / fall back to
`"default"` pair that `Load` and `Save` each already carried.

Result blobs under `image-results/` and `workspace-results/` are untouched: they
are content-addressed by SHA256 of the target, so only the metadata index needed
keying.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`
- [x] `golangci-lint run` — 0 issues
- [x] `go test ./...` — full suite green
- [x] Both new invariants confirmed to bite (context ignored → scoping and
      delete tests fail; lazy migration → ownership test fails)
- [x] `internal/cache` 73.9%, `internal/config` 90.9%
- [ ] `go test -race ./...` — CI
- [ ] **Manual, on your machine:** an existing `~/.devdesk/cache/image-scans.json`
      should keep its entries after first launch and gain the `version`/`contexts`
      wrapper.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	> [!IMPORTANT]
6	> **AI Collaboration Rule**: 
7	> - Support for **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** only.
8	> - **Planning** and **Brainstorming** are handled by Gemini (Antigravity).
9	> - Always refer to [project-context.md](file:///home/anthoni/projects/gitlab/devsecops/devdesk/project-context.md) for global project rules.
10	
11	## Project Overview
12	
13	DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
14	- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
15	- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, clone/pull)
16	- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/misconfig/SBOM + Gitleaks secrets)
17	- Docker container management with real-time metrics
18	- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
19	- Network diagnostics (ICMP, DNS, TCP traceroute, Netcat, HTTP, SSL) + real-time port monitoring
20	- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
21	- Local workspaces management with git metadata
22	
23	## Build and Development Commands
24	
25	Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.
26	
27	```bash
28	# Development (fastest)
29	mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
30	go run .
31	
32	# Build
33	mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
34	mise run run          # Build and run
35	
36	# Testing
37	mise run test         # Run all tests
38	mise run cover        # Coverage per package
39	go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
40	go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
41	mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)
42	
43	# Code Quality
44	mise run fmt          # Format code
45	mise run vet          # Run go vet
46	mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
47	mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
48	mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
49	
50	# Installation
51	mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
52	```
53	
54	`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.
55	
56	## Git workflow — pull requests only
57	
58	**Never push directly to `main`.** The Entire mirror rejects it:
59	
60	```
61	! [remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch)
62	```
63	
64	This is enforced by the mirror, not by GitHub (`gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main`
65	reports `"protected": false`). Every other branch, including
66	`entire/checkpoints/v1`, pushes through the mirror and is forwarded to GitHub.
67	
68	```bash
69	git switch -c <branch>                          # work
70	git push origin <branch>                        # via the mirror — forwarded to GitHub
71	gh pr create --base main --head <branch>
72	gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch
73	git fetch origin && git merge --ff-only origin/main
74	```
75	
76	### Remotes
77	
78	| Remote | URL | Use |
79	|--------|-----|-----|
80	| `origin` | `entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/anthnel/devdesk` | Entire mirror — clone, fetch, push branches |
81	| `github` | `https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk.git` | source of truth; fallback for direct pushes |
82	
83	The repository is hosted on GitHub and mirrored to EntireDB in `aws-eu-central-1`
84	(a second placement exists in `aws-us-east-2`). Prefer `origin` for day-to-day
85	work: it is the regional path and is what keeps agent reads fast.
86	
87	Semantic search (`entire search`, and the `entire:*` skills that depend on it) is
88	**not available in the EU region** — the server answers `semantic search is not
89	yet available in the region(s) hosting this search`. Nothing in the repo config
90	fixes this.
91	
92	## Architecture
93	
94	### Bubble Tea Application Structure
95	
96	This is a **multi-view TUI application** using the Elm Architecture (TEA) pattern via Bubble Tea. Understanding the routing and view lifecycle is critical:
97	
98	**Main Components:**
99	- `main.go` - Entry point, initializes config and Bubble Tea program
100	- `internal/app/app.go` - **Router/orchestrator** that manages view switching and command mode
101	- `internal/app/messages.go` - Cross-view messages (GitLab, scan results, pull, etc.)
102	- `internal/shared/state.go` - SharedState for cross-view data (GitLab client, user, stats)
103	- `internal/ui/*/` - Individual views
104	
105	**Key Architecture Pattern:**
106	```
107	App (Router)
108	├── Manages: currentView, commandMode, viewport, sharedState
109	├── Routes messages to active view
110	├── Handles view switching via command parser
111	├── Manages multi-context configuration
112	└── Views (lazy-loaded):
113	    ├── dashboard       - Overview (stats, tools, service status)
114	    ├── status          - System monitoring (CRUD monitors)
115	    ├── gitlab-auth     - GitLab authentication form
116	    ├── gitlab-explorer - GitLab project/group browser + clone
117	    ├── workspaces      - Local workspace management + git metadata
118	    ├── security        - Trivy + Gitleaks scanner with multi-tab results
119	    ├── containers      - Docker container list + live metrics
120	    ├── oci-resources   - OCI resource list, scan, launch containers, network inspection
121	    └── netdiag         - Network diagnostics (Docker-based tools) + real-time port monitor
122	```
123	
124	### View Switching & Command Mode
125	
126	Press `:` to enter command mode, then type:
127	- `dashboard` or `d` - Switch to dashboard view
128	- `status` or `s` - Switch to status view
129	- `gitlab-auth` or `gla` - Switch to GitLab auth view
130	- `gitlab-explorer` or `gle` - Switch to GitLab explorer view
131	- `workspaces` or `w` - Switch to workspaces view
132	- `security` or `sec` - Switch to security scanner view
133	- `containers` or `c` - Switch to containers view
134	- `oci-resources` or `oci` - Switch to OCI resources view
135	- `netdiag` or `net` - Switch to network diagnostics view
136	- `context <name>` or `ctx <name>` - Switch configuration context
137	- `context list` - Show available contexts
138	- `theme <name>` - Switch UI theme
139	- `quit` - Exit application
140	
141	Command parsing and tab-completion live in `internal/command/`. `ParseCommand()` returns a structured `Command{Type, View, Args}` supporting `CommandView`, `CommandContext`, `CommandTheme`, `CommandQuit`, `CommandUnknown`.
142	
143	**Important:** The `FormView` interface (`InEditMode()`) prevents command mode activation when forms are active. Views with active forms must implement this interface.
144	
145	### Multi-Context Configuration
146	
147	The app supports multiple configuration contexts (e.g., work, personal, client-A):
148	- Contexts are stored in `~/.devdesk/contexts/<name>/config.yaml`
149	- Current context is tracked in `~/.devdesk/current-context`
150	- Each context has isolated GitLab credentials via Git Credential Manager
151	- Context switching reinitializes all views with new config
152	
153	### Configuration System
154	
155	Config loaded from `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` with schema defined in `internal/config/config.go`:
156	- `App` - Global settings (theme, default view, workspaces dir, `secret_backend`)
157	- `Status` - Monitoring settings (refresh interval, components)
158	- `GitLab` - GitLab URL and clone settings
159	- `Registry` - OCI registry configuration (see Registry model below)
160	- `Scan` - Security scanning (Trivy, Gitleaks)
161	
162	**No secret goes in this file.** `GitLabConfig` has no `Token` and
163	`RegistryConfig` has no `Password`; both live in the host secret store (see
164	Credentials Management). Do not add a secret-bearing field back — the schema is
165	what makes the guarantee checkable.
166	
167	Config is injected into views at creation. Use `config.Save()` to persist changes.
168	
169	### Registry model
170	
171	`RegistryConfig.Registries` is one flat list holding both plain registries and
172	repository-manager groups, told apart by `kind` (§3.8). A group fronts several
173	registries and is pullable itself, which is why they share a list.
174

116	// CountFindings aggregates findings into separate counters by source and severity.

118	// Secrets (source "gitleaks"), licenses ("trivy-license"), and misconfigs ("trivy-misconfig")
119	// are counted into their respective dedicated fields.
120	func (r *Result) CountFindings() {
121		r.Counts = SeverityCounts{}
122		r.SecretCount = 0
123		r.LicenseCount = 0
124		r.MisconfigCount = 0

input.new_string:
### 1.1 Fixed

**D27 — the custom tool paths were read by nothing, and the source could not be
chosen. Fixed** by `internal/scan/tool_source.go`, found while planning the
configuration view.

`scan.trivy_path` and `scan.gitleaks_path` were declared in the schema,
defaulted in `Default()`, and tilde-expanded in `ExpandPaths` — and no reader
was ever written. `CheckDependenciesWithImages` called `exec.LookPath("trivy")`
and the command builders hard-coded `toolCmd{Name: "trivy"}` /
`{Name: "gitleaks"}`. Setting a path did nothing, silently. Somebody thought the
field mattered, since it is expanded on load.

The signature is why: the function took the two image names and nothing else, so
there was nowhere to pass a path. The same shape ran through every builder as
the pair `source ToolSource, image string`.

The other half is that resolution tried the binary first and only reached for
Docker in the `else`, so a binary on `PATH` always won: asking for the pinned
image while Trivy happened to be installed was not expressible.

- `ToolSpec{Source, Binary, Image}` replaces the `(source, image)` pair
  everywhere. It is a net *reduction* in argument count — `GetTrivyCommand` had
  eight positional parameters, which is why nobody threaded a ninth through.
- `scan.trivy_source` / `scan.gitleaks_source` take `auto | binary | image`, and
  default to `auto`, which is the historical resolution exactly — an existing
  config cannot change meaning on upgrade.
- **`binary` does not fall back to Docker.** That silent fallback is what kept
  D27 invisible: a path that was never read still produced working scans, run by
  something other than what was asked for.

All three invariants confirmed to bite: ignoring the configured path,
reinstating the Docker fallback, and hard-coding the tool name in the builder
each fail their own test.

**The command line took focus from the render path.** Found in phase 5.

had nowhere to carry a configured path, which is why `trivy_path` sat unread
for so long (D27). Do not add a positional `binary` parameter back; put it on
the spec.

what was asked for.

Phase 0c of `.claude/plans/configuration-view-plan.md`. Independent of #40 and #41.

## The defect

```
config.go   TrivyPath string `yaml:"trivy_path"`   // declared
config.go   TrivyPath: ""                          // defaulted
config.go   c.Scan.TrivyPath = expand(…)           // tilde-expanded on load
                                                   // ← and that is all
scanner.go  exec.LookPath("trivy")                 // hard-coded
gitleaks.go toolCmd{Name: "gitleaks"}              // hard-coded
```

`scan.trivy_path` and `scan.gitleaks_path` had no reader. Setting one did
nothing, silently. Somebody thought the field mattered — it is expanded on load.

**The signature is why.** `CheckDependenciesWithImages(trivyImage, gitleaksImage)`
took the two image names and nothing else, so there was nowhere to pass a path.
The same shape ran through every builder as the pair
`(source ToolSource, image string)`.

## The other half

Resolution tried the binary first and only reached for Docker in the `else`, so
a binary on `PATH` always won. Asking for the pinned image while Trivy happened
to be installed was **not expressible**. "Either the image or the binary" needs a
choice, not two fields configured in the hope the right one is picked.

## What changed

`ToolSpec{Source, Binary, Image}` replaces the `(source, image)` pair
everywhere. It is a net **reduction** in argument count — `GetTrivyCommand` had
eight positional parameters, which is why nobody threaded a ninth through for
the binary path.

```yaml
scan:
  trivy_source: auto      # auto | binary | image
  trivy_path: ""
  trivy_image: aquasec/trivy
  gitleaks_source: auto
```

| Value | Resolution |
|---|---|
| `auto` (default) | the binary when there is one, the image otherwise — **exactly** the old behaviour |
| `binary` | `trivy_path` when set, else the name on `PATH`; **fails rather than falling back to Docker** |
| `image` | `trivy_image`, even when a binary is installed |

`auto` being the default and the applied default for an empty value means **no
existing config changes meaning on upgrade** — pinned by
`TestAutoKeepsTheOldBinaryFirstResolution`.

### Why `binary` fails loudly

The silent Docker fallback is what kept D27 invisible: an unread path still
produced working scans, run by something other than what was asked for. A tool
that was asked for and is not there is now an unavailable tool, which the
dashboard already reports.

## Confirmed to bite

Each of the three invariants was broken on purpose before the fix was kept:

| Sabotage | Failure |
|---|---|
| ignore `configuredPath` | `trivy at …\trivy.exe was not found; a configured path is the one thing that must be looked at` |
| reinstate the Docker fallback | `trivy reported available (source "docker") with source=binary and no binary anywhere` |
| hard-code the tool name in the builder | `command runs "trivy", want the configured binary` |

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`
- [x] `golangci-lint run` — 0 issues
- [x] `go test ./...` — full suite green
- [x] `internal/scan` 98.8%, `internal/config` 92.0%
- [ ] `go test -race ./...` — CI
- [ ] **Manual:** `scan.trivy_source: image` with trivy installed should show
      Trivy as `docker:` in the dashboard tool list.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

Les trois phases 0 sont livrées, en trois PR indépendantes.

| PR | Phase | Contenu |
|---|---|---|
| **#40** | 0 | `scan.OptionsFromConfig` — **D26** |
| **#41** | 0b | caches de scan par contexte |
| **#42** | 0c | `ToolSpec` + source `auto\|binary\|image` — **D27** |

Toutes trois branchées sur `main`, sans chevauchement de fichiers — mergeables dans n'importe quel ordre.

## Ce que 0c a révélé en plus du plan

Le plan disait « passer `DependencyStatus` entier plutôt qu'un neuvième argument ». En écrivant, une meilleure forme est apparue : `ToolSpec` **remplace** le couple `(source ToolSource, image string)` qui traversait tous les constructeurs. C'est une *réduction* du nombre d'arguments, pas un ajout — et c'est ce qui explique le défaut rétrospectivement. `GetTrivyCommand` avait huit paramètres positionnels ; personne n'allait en enfiler un neuvième pour un chemin.

Un point que je n'avais pas anticipé : `ScanOptions` a dû gagner `TrivySource`/`TrivyPath`/`GitleaksSource`/`GitleaksPath`, parce que `NewScanner` fait la détection lui-même. Les noms correspondent exactement à ceux de `ScanConfig` — donc quand #40 sera mergée, son test par réflexion **exigera** que `OptionsFromConfig` les transporte. Les deux PR se renforcent au lieu d'entrer en conflit.

## Les trois sabotages de 0c

| Sabotage | Message |
|---|---|
| chemin configuré ignoré | `a configured path is the one thing that must be looked at` |
| repli Docker rétabli | `trivy reported available (source "docker") with source=binary and no binary anywhere` |
| nom d'outil en dur | `command runs "trivy", want the configured binary` |

`auto` est la valeur par défaut **et** la valeur appliquée quand le champ est vide, donc aucune config existante ne change de sens à la montée de version — `TestAutoKeepsTheOldBinaryFirstResolution` l'épingle.

`internal/scan` 98.8 %, `internal/config` 92.0 %, `internal/cache` 73.9 %, lint 0 issue partout.

## Deux vérifications qui demandent ta machine

- **#41** : un `~/.devdesk/cache/image-scans.json` existant doit garder ses entrées au premier lancement et gagner l'enveloppe `version`/`contexts`.
- **#42** : `scan.trivy_source: image` avec trivy installé doit afficher Trivy en `docker:` dans la liste d'outils du dashboard.

La phase 1 — la vue configuration elle-même — attend que tu aies mergé, puisqu'elle s'appuie sur 0 et 0c.

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	> [!IMPORTANT]
6	> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
7	> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all

13	
14	## Project Overview
15	
16	DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
17	- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
18	- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, clone/pull)
19	- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/misconfig/SBOM + Gitleaks secrets)
20	- Docker container management with real-time metrics
21	- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
22	- Network diagnostics (ICMP, DNS, TCP traceroute, Netcat, HTTP, SSL) + real-time port monitoring
23	- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
24	- Local workspaces management with git metadata
25	
26	## Build and Development Commands
27	
28	Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.
29	
30	```bash
31	# Development (fastest)
32	mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
33	go run .
34	
35	# Build
36	mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
37	mise run run          # Build and run
38	
39	# Testing
40	mise run test         # Run all tests
41	mise run cover        # Coverage per package
42	go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
43	go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
44	mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)
45	
46	# Code Quality
47	mise run fmt          # Format code
48	mise run vet          # Run go vet
49	mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
50	mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
51	mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
52	
53	# Installation
54	mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
55	```
56	
57	`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.
58	
59	## Git workflow — pull requests only
60	
61	**Never push directly to `main`.** The Entire mirror rejects it:
62	
63	```
64	! [remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch)
65	```
66	
67	This is enforced by the mirror, not by GitHub (`gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main`
68	reports `"protected": false`). Every other branch, including
69	`entire/checkpoints/v1`, pushes through the mirror and is forwarded to GitHub.
70	
71	```bash
72	git switch -c <branch>                          # work
73	git push origin <branch>                        # via the mirror — forwarded to GitHub
74	gh pr create --base main --head <branch>
75	gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch
76	git fetch origin && git merge --ff-only origin/main
77	```
78	
79	### Remotes
80	
81	| Remote | URL | Use |
82	|--------|-----|-----|
83	| `origin` | `entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/anthnel/devdesk` | Entire mirror — clone, fetch, push branches |
84	| `github` | `https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk.git` | source of truth; fallback for direct pushes |
85	
86	The repository is hosted on GitHub and mirrored to EntireDB in `aws-eu-central-1`
87	(a second placement exists in `aws-us-east-2`). Prefer `origin` for day-to-day
88	work: it is the regional path and is what keeps agent reads fast.
89	
90	Semantic search (`entire search`, and the `entire:*` skills that depend on it) is
91	**not available in the EU region** — the server answers `semantic search is not
92	yet available in the region(s) hosting this search`. Nothing in the repo config
93	fixes this.
94	
95	## Architecture
96	
97	### Bubble Tea Application Structure
98	
99	This is a **multi-view TUI application** using the Elm Architecture (TEA) pattern via Bubble Tea. Understanding the routing and view lifecycle is critical:
100	
101	**Main Components:**
102	- `main.go` - Entry point, initializes config and Bubble Tea program
103	- `internal/app/app.go` - **Router/orchestrator** that manages view switching and command mode
104	- `internal/app/messages.go` - Cross-view messages (GitLab, scan results, pull, etc.)
105	- `internal/shared/state.go` - SharedState for cross-view data (GitLab client, user, stats)
106	- `internal/ui/*/` - Individual views
107	
108	**Key Architecture Pattern:**
109	```
110	App (Router)
111	├── Manages: currentView, commandMode, viewport, sharedState
112	├── Routes messages to active view
113	├── Handles view switching via command parser
114	├── Manages multi-context configuration
115	└── Views (lazy-loaded):
116	    ├── dashboard       - Overview (stats, tools, service status)
117	    ├── status          - System monitoring (CRUD monitors)
118	    ├── gitlab-auth     - GitLab authentication form
119	    ├── gitlab-explorer - GitLab project/group browser + clone
120	    ├── workspaces      - Local workspace management + git metadata
121	    ├── security        - Trivy + Gitleaks scanner with multi-tab results
122	    ├── containers      - Docker container list + live metrics
123	    ├── oci-resources   - OCI resource list, scan, launch containers, network inspection
124	    └── netdiag         - Network diagnostics (Docker-based tools) + real-time port monitor
125	```
126	
127	### View Switching & Command Mode
128	
129	Press `:` to enter command mode, then type:
130	- `dashboard` or `d` - Switch to dashboard view
131	- `status` or `s` - Switch to status view
132	- `gitlab-auth` or `gla` - Switch to GitLab auth view
133	- `gitlab-explorer` or `gle` - Switch to GitLab explorer view
134	- `workspaces` or `w` - Switch to workspaces view
135	- `security` or `sec` - Switch to security scanner view
136	- `containers` or `c` - Switch to containers view
137	- `oci-resources` or `oci` - Switch to OCI resources view
138	- `netdiag` or `net` - Switch to network diagnostics view
139	- `context <name>` or `ctx <name>` - Switch configuration context
140	- `context list` - Show available contexts
141	- `theme <name>` - Switch UI theme
142	- `quit` - Exit application
143	
144	Command parsing and tab-completion live in `internal/command/`. `ParseCommand()` returns a structured `Command{Type, View, Args}` supporting `CommandView`, `CommandContext`, `CommandTheme`, `CommandQuit`, `CommandUnknown`.
145	
146	**Important:** The `FormView` interface (`InEditMode()`) prevents command mode activation when forms are active. Views with active forms must implement this interface.
147	
148	### Multi-Context Configuration
149	
150	The app supports multiple configuration contexts (e.g., work, personal, client-A):
151	- Contexts are stored in `~/.devdesk/contexts/<name>/config.yaml`
152	- Current context is tracked in `~/.devdesk/current-context`
153	- Each context has isolated GitLab credentials via Git Credential Manager
154	- Context switching reinitializes all views with new config
155	
156	### Configuration System
157	
158	Config loaded from `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` with schema defined in `internal/config/config.go`:
159	- `App` - Global settings (theme, default view, workspaces dir, `secret_backend`)
160	- `Status` - Monitoring settings (refresh interval, components)
161	- `GitLab` - GitLab URL and clone settings
162	- `Registry` - OCI registry configuration (see Registry model below)
163	- `Scan` - Security scanning (Trivy, Gitleaks)
164	
165	**No secret goes in this file.** `GitLabConfig` has no `Token` and
166	`RegistryConfig` has no `Password`; both live in the host secret store (see
167	Credentials Management). Do not add a secret-bearing field back — the schema is
168	what makes the guarantee checkable.
169	
170	Config is injected into views at creation. Use `config.Save()` to persist changes.

## Ce qui s'est passé au merge

Deux choses valent d'être notées.

**Le test de #40 a attrapé #42.** Au moment de fusionner les deux, `TestEveryConfiguredOptionReachesTheScanner` a échoué sur les quatre champs que #42 avait ajoutés :

```
